A light oil rubbed on clothing and bare skin, making the user ethereal 3 rounds after it is applied. Ethereal, the user can pass through solid objects in any direction, or travel to other planes, but cannot touch non-ethereal things, and is invisible. It lasts 4 + 1-4 turns, unless washed off earlier with a weak acidic solution. It can be put on objects as well as creatures; one potion covers a normal human and the gear he or she usually carries (2 or 3 weapons, clothing, armor, shield and the usual miscellaneous gear). (Cf. the phase door spell, and TRAVEL IN THE KNOWN PLANES OF EXISTENCE hereafter.)

(A roper could still cause weakness, but its tentacles could not wrap around the oiled person.) Webs, magical or not, do not affect the user, and bonds such as ropes, manacles and chains can be slipped. Magical ropes and the like do not work against it. Poured on a floor or steps, it gives a 95% chance per round that creatures standing there slip and fall. It wears off after 8 hours, or can be wiped off with an alcohol solution (such as wine).

The wearer will never harm himself or herself: if others suggest that the wearer should be sure to defend against attacks, or should not strike his or her own head, the wearer agrees (and may attack or strike at the speaker’s head), since the contrary result is obvious in that case. Rubbing the ring sends the summons, and the djinni appears the next round. It faithfully obeys and serves the wearer, but if the ring’s servant is ever killed, the ring becomes non-magical and worthless. See 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, for a djinni’s abilities.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · DMG C, UA III.C

The 4 types (air, earth, fire, water) are very powerful. Each looks like a lesser ring (given below) but has other powers, plus these common properties:

  1. Elementals of the ring’s plane cannot come within 5’ of the wearer or attack him or her. Or the wearer may give up this protection and try to charm the elemental (saving throw at −2). If the charm fails, the protection is lost and no further charm attempt is possible, but the secondary properties below still work against the elemental.
  2. Creatures of the ring’s plane, other than normal elementals, attack the wearer at −1 “to hit”; the wearer takes −1 per hit die of damage from them and saves at +2 against their attacks; the wearer attacks them at +4 “to hit” (or −4 on the elemental creature’s saving throw) and does +6 damage (total, not per die), adjusted by any other bonuses and/or penalties. Any weapon the wearer uses can hit elementals or elemental creatures even if not magical.
  3. The wearer can talk with the elementals or elemental creatures of the ring’s plane. They recognize the ring and will at least show healthy respect. If their alignment is opposed, this becomes fear if the wearer is strong, or hatred and a desire to kill if the wearer is weak.
  4. The owner suffers a saving throw penalty: Air −2 vs. fire; Earth −2 vs. petrification; Fire −2 vs. water or cold; Water −2 vs. lightning/electricity.
  5. Only one power (major or minor) of the ring can be in use at a time.

Air: gust of wind (once per round); fly; wall of force (once per day); control winds (once per week); invisibility. It looks like nothing more than an invisibility ring until a certain condition is met (such as having it blessed, slaying an air elemental, or whatever the DM decides is needed to unlock its full power).

Earth: stone tell (once per day); passwall (twice per day); wall of stone (once per day); stone to flesh (twice per week); move earth (once per week); feather fall. It looks like a ring of feather falling until the condition is met.

Fire: burning hands (once per turn); pyrotechnics (twice per day); wall of fire (once per day); flame strike (twice per week); fire resistance. It looks like a ring of fire resistance until the condition is met.

Water: purify water; create water (once per day); water breathing (5’ radius); wall of ice (once per day); airy water; lower water (twice per week); part water (twice per week); water walking. It looks like a ring of water walking until the condition is met.

The powers work at 12th level of experience, or the minimum level for the equivalent spell if higher, for range, duration and area. The additional powers take only 5 segments to use.

  • Exceptionally hot fires (red dragon breath, pyrohydra breath, fireballs, flame strike, fire storm, etc.) are saved against at +4, and damage is −2 per die, but never less than 1 per die.

(As a rule of thumb, very hot fires are those with a maximum initial exposure of up to 24 hit points; exceptionally hot, 25 or more.)

It does not allow breathing water without other magic.

There are 2 kinds; roll percentile dice: 01-90 = ring of regeneration, 91-00 = vampiric regeneration ring. In either case, the wearer’s hit points can never go above the total first rolled.

Regeneration: restores 1 hit point of damage per turn, and eventually regrows lost limbs or organs too. It even brings the wearer back from death (but if poison was the cause, the saving throw must be made or the wearer dies again from the poison still in his or her system). Only total destruction of all living tissue by fire, acid or similar means prevents regeneration. It must be worn; taking it off stops the process.

Vampiric regeneration (rare): the wearer immediately gains one-half of the damage he or she does to opponents in hand-to-hand combat (melee, not missiles or spells), fractions dropped. It gives no other regeneration and does not restore life, limbs or organs.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG C, UA III.C

Has 2 modes, both working only in relative darkness. Range, duration and area are the minimum for the comparable spell unless stated otherwise, and each function takes 5 segments.

At night under the open sky:

  • dancing lights (once per hour), as the spell;
  • light (twice per night), 12” range, as the spell;
  • ball lightning (once per night), see below;
  • shooting stars (special), see below.

Ball lightning: releases 1 to 4 balls of lightning, as the wearer chooses, looking exactly like dancing lights and controlled the same way. They have a 12” range and 4 round duration, move 4” per round, and are about 3’ across. Any creature a ball touches or comes near discharges it (a save versus magic halves the damage, since the contact was across an air gap). They can be released together or one at a time, within 1 round or as needed through the night. Damage per ball: 4 balls, 2-8 hit points each; 3 balls, 2-12 each; 2 balls, 5-20 each; 1 ball, 4-48.

Shooting stars: glowing missiles with fiery trails, much like a meteor swarm; 3 can be released each week, together or one at a time. Each flies straight up to 7” and bursts at the end of its range unless it hits an object or creature first. A creature hit takes 12 hit points from the impact plus 24 from the burst (as a fireball, in a 1” diameter sphere). Creatures within the burst save versus magic for half (12 hit points), otherwise taking the full 24. A creature in the missile’s path must save versus magic or be hit, at −3 within 2” of the wearer, −1 from 2” to 4”, normal beyond 4”.

Indoors at night, or underground:

  • faerie fire (twice per day), as the spell;
  • spark shower (once per day): a flying cloud of sizzling purple sparks fanning out 20’ from the ring to a width of 10’. Creatures in it take 2-8 hit points of damage each, or 4-16 if wearing metal armor or holding a metal weapon.

  1. Area spells not cast directly at the wearer are not turned.
  2. Spells delivered by touch are not turned.
  3. Magic from devices (rods, staves, wands, rings and other items) triggered without spell casting is not turned. A scroll spell does not count as a device.

How much is turned: roll percentile dice and round to the nearest 10 (1-5 drops, 6-9 adds 10, so 05 is 0%, but 96 is 100%). That percentage of the spell rebounds on its caster, and damage is divided in proportion. Both parties’ saving throws improve by +1 for each 10% below 100% (80% = +2, 70% = +3, . . . 10% = +9). Even so, both the target and the caster may end up polymorphed into bullfrogs!

Spells with no saving throw: unless the turning roll is 09 or less or 91 or more, the ring allows a saving throw against spells that normally have none, negating them or halving damage as appropriate. For each 10% turned, allow a 5% (1 in 20) chance: if 11-19 is rolled, a 20 saves; 20-29 allows a 19-20 to save; 30-39 allows 18-20; and so on. Example: an illusionist casts maze on a fighter wearing the ring, and 34% is turned. The fighter has a 15% chance to save; otherwise the maze takes full effect. The illusionist must also save (100% − 34% = 66%, or 6 10% steps, giving a 30% chance) by rolling 15-20 or be mazed too. A save here negates the spell. This special saving throw is NOT modified by race, magic items or any other condition, including spells already in effect.

Spells that affect a set number of levels, aimed at the wearer, must be able to affect as many levels as the wearer and caster have together; if so, the procedure above decides the final effect.

To receive a spell willingly, the wearer must take off the ring. Psionic attacks are not spell casting.

system.description:
Protects the wearer from all divination and from mental or magical location and/or detection: clairaudience, clairvoyance, ESP, telepathy, crystal balls and all other scrying devices. No aura can be seen on the wearer, and no predictions can be made about him or her unless some powerful being is consulted.

Experience points 4,000 · Sale value 15,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

When first found it certainly looks like a large iron barrel. A secret catch opens a hatch in one end, and inside are 10 levers:

  1. extend legs and tail/retract same
  2. uncover forward porthole/cover same
  3. uncover side portholes/cover same
  4. extend pincers and feelers/retract same
  5. snap pincers
  6. forward/left or right
  7. backwards/left or right
  8. open “eyes” with continual light inside/close “eyes”
  9. raise (levitate)/sink
  10. open hatch/close hatch

It moves forward at 3”, backward at 6”. Its 2 pincers reach 4’ forward and snap for 2-12 hit points of damage each if they hit a creature: a 25% chance, with no reduction for armor, but dexterity reduction applies. It works in water up to 900’ deep, holds 2 human-sized people, and carries enough air for 2-5 hours at full capacity. It is AC 0; 100 hit points of damage make it leak, and 200 stave in a side. Fully working, it looks something like a giant lobster.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 35,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Usually looks like a normal (or possibly magic) arrow, but works much like a locate object spell, showing the way to what is asked. Once per day it can be tossed in the air, and it falls pointing the way; this can be repeated 7 times over the next 7 turns. It points only to the way or place asked for, and the request can only be for a stairway (up or down), sloping passage (up or down), dungeon exit or entrance, cave or cavern. Requests must be phrased by distance (nearest, farthest, highest, lowest) or by direction (north, south, east, west, etc.).

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 17,500 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

A heavy cloth bag about 2’ wide and 4’ long (like any other bag or large sack), holding several large pebble-like objects. If they are dumped out, each explodes for 5-20 hit points of damage, and every creature within 10’ must save versus magic or take full damage. To be removed safely, the beans must be taken out by hand; telekinesis will not work, nor will any use of tools that does not set them off.

Each bean must be planted in dirt and watered, and from each in turn springs some creature or thing. 3-12 beans is suggested, with only 1 or 2 beneficial and the rest monsters or useless things. For example:

  1. 3 shriekers spring up and begin wailing.
  2. An ice storm strikes the area.
  3. A poisonous raspberry bush with animated runners shoots up, but each of its 5-20 berries is a gem of 100 or 500 g.p. base value (or perhaps just worthless glass).
  4. A hole opens in the ground; a purple worm might be below, or a djinni ring . . .
  5. Smoke and gases cover a 50’ radius for 5 turns; creatures inside cannot see and are blinded for 1-6 rounds even after leaving the cloud.
  6. A wyvern grows instantly and attacks; its sting is a javelin of piercing.
  7. Poison gas seeps out slowly, forming a 20’ radius cloud lasting 1 turn; meanwhile it might turn some dirt at its center into magic dust (appearance, vanishing, sneezing and choking . . . ).

Thought, imagination and judgment are needed with this item.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 5,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Looks like a typical sack, perhaps empty, perhaps with beans in the bottom, but it is really the lure of an extra-dimensional creature, one of its feeding mouths. It radiates magic. Any animal or plant matter thrust inside may be “swallowed”.

It is 90% likely to ignore the first intrusions, but whenever it senses living human flesh inside, it is 60% likely to close and try to draw the whole victim in: a base 75% chance, less 5% per +1 of strength damage bonus (or plus 5% per −1). An 18 strength character (+2 damage) is only 65% likely to be drawn in; a 5 strength character (−1 damage) is 80% likely. Creatures drawn in are eaten in 7 segments and gone forever.

It holds up to 30 cubic feet and acts as a bag of holding (normal capacity), but each turn there is a 5% cumulative chance it “swallows” its contents and “spits them out” into some non-space.

Looks like a jug or flask: a magical beaker that brews 2-5 doses of 2-5 kinds of potion, decided at random when first found. The kinds are layered inside, and each pouring takes 1 round and gives 1 dose of 1 kind.

Roll d4 + 1 for the number of potions, then roll for each one (delusion and poison are possible, and so are duplicates), recording them in order. With 2 potions, it pours each 1 per day, 3 times per week; with 3, each 1 per day, 2 times per week; with 4 or 5, each only 1 time per week. Once opened, it slowly loses its power, permanently losing one kind of potion per month.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 12,500 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Always found as a small wooden “box” about 1’ long, ½’ wide and ½’ deep, which radiates magic if detection is possible. The “box” can hold other things.

  • First command word: it unfolds into a boat 10’ long, 4’ wide and 2’ deep, with 1 pair of oars, an anchor, a mast and a lateen sail. It holds 3 or 4 people comfortably.
  • Second (different) word: it unfolds into a ship 24’ long, 8’ wide and 6’ deep: decked, with single rowing seats, 5 sets of oars, a steering oar, anchor, deck cabin, mast and square sail. It carries 15 people easily.
  • Third word: it folds back into a box.

The DM may have the command words written, visibly or invisibly, on the box, or elsewhere (perhaps on an item inside), or simply lost, needing a search (legend lore, a sage, searching the dungeon, etc.) to find them.

Experience points 10,000 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

A holy book sacred to good clerics. Reading it takes 1 week. Its effect depends on the reader:

  • Good cleric: gains 1 point of wisdom and enough experience points to be exactly half way into the next level.
  • Cleric neither good nor evil: loses 20,000-80,000 experience points (a negative total is possible, needing restoration, but level never drops below 1st).
  • Evil cleric: loses 1 full level, dropping to the lowest experience total for that level, and must atone by magical means, or by giving up 50% of everything gained for 2-5 adventures (losing the matching experience points too), or gain no more experience.
  • Fighter: unaffected, though a paladin feels it to be good.
  • Magic-user: loses 1 point of intelligence unless he or she saves versus magic; on a save, loses 2,000-20,000 experience points instead.
  • Thief: takes 5-30 hit points of damage and must save versus magic or lose 1 point of dexterity; if wisdom is 15 or higher, there is also a 10%-60% chance of giving up thieving to become a good cleric.
  • Assassin: takes 5-40 hit points of damage and must save versus magic or commit suicide.
  • Monk: not harmed, and cannot understand it.
  • Bard: treated as a neutral cleric, losing experience from bard experience only.

Except as noted, it cannot be told apart from any other magic book, libram, tome, etc. by its cover or by looking it over; it must be read. (This is also true of the other magical writings described hereafter.) Once read, it vanishes forever, and the same player character can never benefit from reading another.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Gives its owner the ability to use spells. On first reading it, any character not already able to use spells takes 5-20 hit points of damage and is stunned for 5-20 turns; after that he or she can read it without harm.

Pages: it has 23-30 (22 + d8) pages, each rolled randomly:

01-30 blank page
31-50 cleric spell
51-60 druid spell
61-95 magic-user spell

For a spell, roll d10 for its level (d12 for magic-user spells); on 8-10 (or 10-12 for magic-user), roll d6 instead (d8 for magic-user spells). Then pick the spell at random. Record the pages secretly, and DO NOT REVEAL THIS INFORMATION TO THE HOLDER OF THE BOOK.

Using it: pages can only be turned forward, never back, and when the last page is turned, the book vanishes. The owner can cast the spell on the page the book is open to once per day, or up to 4 times per day if it is a spell the character could normally cast by class and level. The book need not be with the owner to give this power, so it can be kept somewhere safe during adventures. Use the spell just as if from a scroll, including casting time, spell failure, etc.

Turning pages: each time a spell is cast, its energy may magically turn the page (despite all precautions); the owner knows when this happens, and may even benefit by gaining a new spell. The chances:

Experience points 9,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

A work of unspeakable evil, meat and drink to evil clerics. Reading it fully takes 1 week. Its effect depends on the reader:

  • Evil cleric: gains 1 point of wisdom and enough experience points to be exactly half way into the next level.
  • Cleric neither good nor evil: 50% chance of losing 30,000-120,000 experience points, otherwise becomes evil without benefit from the book.
  • Good cleric: must save versus poison or die. If he or she survives, must save versus magic or go permanently insane; even if that save succeeds, loses 250,000 experience points, less 10,000 per point of wisdom.
  • Other good characters: take 5-30 hit points of damage from handling it, and if they look inside there is an 80% chance a night hag (q.v.) comes to attack them that night.
  • Neutral (not evil) characters: take 5-20 hit points of damage from handling it; reading it means saving versus poison or becoming evil, immediately seeking out an evil cleric to confirm the new alignment.

(Cf. Book of Exalted Deeds for other details.)

In melee, or while fleeing from it, they hinder movement and start to tap and shuffle, heel and toe, or shuffle off to Buffalo, so the wearer acts exactly as if under irresistible dance (−4 on armor class, no saving throws, no attacks). Once their true nature shows, only remove curse lets them be taken off.

Experience points --- · Sale value 5,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Soft boots that let the wearer move with no sound of footsteps in almost any surroundings. The wearer can cross dry leaves or a normally creaky wooden floor making only a whisper of noise: say a 95% chance of silence in the worst conditions, 100% in the best.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 5,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Like other magic boots, these soft boots fit feet from giant to halfling size. The wearer can rise or descend straight up or down at will, at 20’ per round (minute), with no limit on use. The weight they can lift is 280 pounds plus d20 × 14 pounds, so a given pair lifts 294 to 560 pounds. An ogre could wear them, but would be too heavy to levitate. (Cf. the second level magic-user spell levitation.)

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 15,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

The wearer can run as fast as a fast horse: 24” base movement. Each 10 pounds (100 g.p. equivalent) over 200 pounds slows the wearer 1”: a 180 pound human with 60 pounds of gear moves 20”, and carrying a sack of 500 gold pieces as well slows him another 5”. For every hour of continuous fast movement, the wearer must rest 1 hour, and no more than 8 hours of continuous fast movement are possible before resting. In combat where such movement is possible, they give +2 to armor class.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 20,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Striding: the wearer has a base movement of 12” whatever his or her size or weight, and can keep it up tirelessly for up to 12 hours per day; after that the boots stop working for 12 hours while they “recharge”.

Springing: “normal” paces are 3’, but the wearer can jump up to 30’ forward, 9’ backward and 15’ straight up. Where circumstances allow, the wearer can strike and spring away in combat when he or she has the initiative. This is risky: there is a base 20% chance of stumbling and being stunned the next round, less 3% per point of dexterity above 12 (17% at 13, 14% at 14, 11% at 15, 8% at 16, 5% at 17, and just 2% at 18).

In any case the quick movement improves the wearer’s armor class by 1 (AC 2 becomes 1, AC 1 becomes 0, etc.).

When it is filled with water (fresh or salt) and certain words are spoken (taking 1 round), a 12 hit dice water elemental appears. With salt water the elemental is stronger (+2 per hit die, but no more than 8 h.p. per die). For control and other details see Elemental in 1e Fantasy RPG, MM. (Cf. bowl of watery death below.)

Experience points 4,000 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E1, UA III.E.1

Looks exactly like a bowl commanding water elementals, including color, design, magic radiation, etc. But when it is filled with water, the magic-user must save versus magic (at −2 if salt water is used) or be shrunk to the size of a small ant and plunged into the middle of the bowl.

The victim drowns in 3-8 rounds unless saved by magic, since he or she cannot be physically removed from the bowl. Only animal growth, enlarge or wish will free the victim and restore normal size; a growth potion poured into the water does the same; a sweet water potion gives the victim another saving throw (a chance that the curse works only briefly). A victim who drowns is permanently dead: no resurrection is possible, and even a wish will not work.

system.description:

A hollow mithral tube about 1’ long. Struck, it sends out magical vibrations that open locks, lids, doors, valves and portals, and work against normal bars, shackles, chains, bolts, etc. It also destroys a hold portal spell, or even a wizard lock cast by a magic-user below 15th level.

It must be pointed at the item or gate to be opened, then struck. A clear chime rings out (which may attract monsters), and within 1 round 1 function is done: a lock opened, a shackle loosened, a secret door opened, a chest lid lifted, etc. A chest that is chained, padlocked, locked and wizard locked takes 4 or 5 soundings. A silence spell negates it. It has 20-80 (20 + d6 × 10) charges before it cracks and becomes useless.

Experience points 3,500 · Sale value 20,000 gp · DMG E2, UA III.E.2

Spells: comprehend languages, read magic, infravision and tongues cast on the user can improve his or her viewing. Detect magic and detect evil/good can be cast through the ball, with a 5% chance per level of the magic-user of working correctly.

Noticing the scrying: only creatures with intelligence 12 or better have a chance. The base chance depends on class: fighter 2%, thief 6%, paladin 6%, assassin 5%, ranger 4%, monk 1%, bard 3%. Each point of intelligence above 12 adds a further cumulative chance, growing arithmetically from 1%: 1%, 3%, 6%, 10%, 15%, 21% at 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 intelligence. Add 1% per level of experience as well. Treat monsters as the most similar of these. Check each round of scrying; a roll of the percentage or less means the subject knows it is being watched. If a spell user (cleric, druid, magic-user or illusionist) is being watched, use the DETECTION OF INVISIBILITY table on page 60 instead, checking each round.

Dispel magic makes the crystal ball stop working for 1 day. The various protections against crystal ball viewing just leave it hazy and not working. (The DM may allow scrying devices for clerics and druids; water basins and mirrors are suggested, working as normal crystal balls.)

Usually found in a box or leather pouch: a deck of thin plaques of ivory or vellum, each engraved and/or inscribed with glyphs, characters and magical sigils. The moment a plaque is drawn, its magic falls on the person who drew it, for better or worse.

Drawing: the owner announces before the first draw how many plaques he or she will draw: 1, 2, 3 or even 4. Drawing the jester allows 2 extra draws if the owner wishes. Each plaque drawn goes back in the deck, except the jester and fool, which are discarded. The deck has 13 plaques (75%) or 22 (25%); the extra ones in a 22-card deck are marked * below. Normal playing cards can stand in for them as shown. The deck vanishes when the last possible plaque is drawn, or at once if The Void or Donjon (printed in bold face) is drawn.

Plaque (card)Effect
Sun (KD)Gain beneficial miscellaneous magic item and 50,000 experience points
Moon (QD)You are granted 1-4 wishes

*Comet (2D)Defeat the next monster you meet to gain 1 level

Knight (JH)Gain the service of a 4th level fighter
*Gem (2H)Gain your choice of 20 jewelry or 50 gems
The Void (KC)Body functions, but soul is trapped elsewhere
Flames (QC)Enmity between you and a devil
Skull (JC)Defeat Death or be forever destroyed
*Talons (2C)All magic items you possess are torn from you
Ruin (KS)Immediately lose all wealth and real property
Euryale (QS)Minus 3 on all saving throws vs. petrification
Rogue (JS)One of your henchmen turns against you
*Balance (2S)Change alignment or be judged
Jester (J)Gain 10,000 experience points or 2 more draws from the deck
*Fool (J with Trademark)Lose 10,000 experience points; draw again
*Vizier (AD)Know the answer to your next dilemma
*Idiot (AD)Lose 1-4 points of intelligence, you may draw again
*Fates (AH)Avoid any situation you choose . . . once
*Donjon (AS)You are imprisoned

The plaques explained:

  • Sun: roll on the MISCELLANEOUS MAGIC TABLE (III.E., 1.-5.) until a useful item (not an artifact or relic) comes up. The player gets experience points for it too.
  • Moon: best shown as a moonstone with the number of wishes as gleams in it. They are the same as the ninth level magic-user spell (q.v.), and must be used within as many turns as the number received.
  • Star: if the 2 points would raise the score to 19, put 1 or both into other abilities in this order: constitution, charisma, wisdom, dexterity, intelligence, strength.
  • Comet: the character must single-handedly defeat the next hostile monster (one or several) or lose the benefit. If successful, he or she moves to the mid-point of the next level.
  • Throne: if charisma is already 18, the character still gains +25% on encounter and loyalty reactions, and becomes a real leader in people’s eyes. The castle gained is near any stronghold already owned.
  • Key: roll a treasure map with +20% on the dice. The weapon must be usable by the character, so use the SWORDS (III.G.), MISCELLANEOUS WEAPONS (III.H.) or RODS, et al. (III.D.) table as needed.
  • Knight: the hero joins as the character’s henchman and serves loyally until death. He has +1 per die (18 maximum) on each ability roll.
  • Gem: wealth. The jewelry is all gold set with gems, and the gems are all of 1,000 g.p. base value. Experience points equal to the value come with it, but never more than enough for 1 level rise.
  • The Void: this lightless black plaque means instant disaster. The character’s body functions and speaks like an automaton, but the soul is trapped in a prison somewhere: in an object on a far planet or plane, possibly owned by a demon. A wish will not bring the character back, but might reveal the plane of imprisonment.
  • Flames: hot anger, jealousy and envy are just some of the possible motives for the enmity. The devil is usually of the Greater sort, possibly even an Arch-devil. The enmity can never end until one or the other is slain.
  • Skull: a minor Death appears (AC −4; 33 hit points; strikes with a scythe for 2-16 hit points, never missing, always striking first in a round), and the character must fight it alone; if others help, they get minor Deaths to fight as well. A character slain by it is slain forever. Treat the Death as undead for spells. Cold, fire and electrical energy do not harm it.
  • Talons: every magic item the character owns or holds is instantly and permanently gone.
  • Ruin: all money (including gems, jewelry and other precious and valuable treasure and art), and all real property and buildings currently owned, are lost forever.
  • Euryale: the medusa-like face brings a curse that only the Fates card or god-like beings can remove; otherwise the −3 is permanent.
  • Rogue: 1 of the character’s henchmen becomes totally alienated and hostile forever. If there are no henchmen, the enmity of some powerful personage (community or religious) can be used instead. The hatred stays secret until the time is ripe for devastating effect.
  • Balance: “weighed in the balance and found wanting”, the character must change to a radically different alignment (lawful-chaotic, good-evil, neutral-non-neutral) and act accordingly. Failure brings judgment, and if the character deviates substantially from the professed alignment, he or she is permanently destroyed.
  • Jester: makes either deck more beneficial if the experience award is taken. It is always discarded when drawn, like the Fool and unlike all others.
  • Fool: the payment and draw are mandatory!
  • Vizier: the character can call on supernatural wisdom to solve any single problem or fully answer any question, whenever he or she asks. Whether the answer can be acted on successfully is another matter entirely.
  • Idiot: the mongoloid face causes the immediate loss of 1-4 (d4) points of intelligence, which cannot be regained (though points can be restored by other means). The extra draw is optional.
  • Fates: the character can avoid even an instantaneous event if desired, since the fabric of reality is unraveled and respun, so to speak. It can only stop something happening, not make something happen, and only for that character; the party must still face the confrontation.
  • Donjon: imprisonment, by spell or by some creature/being as the DM chooses. All gear and spells are stripped from the victim in any case.

All figurines share these traits: each looks like a small statuette only an inch or so high, but when it is tossed down and a command word spoken, it becomes a living creature that obeys and serves its owner. A figurine destroyed in statuette form is ruined forever, its magic gone. One slain in animal form just turns back into a statuette and can be used again later, as long as the statuette is not broken. Roll for the type:

01-15 ebony fly
16-30 golden lions (pair)
31-40 ivory goats (trio)
41-55 marble elephant
56-65 obsidian steed
66-85 onyx dog
86-00 serpentine owl

Ebony fly: grows to the size of a pony: armor class 4, 4 + 4 hit dice, air maneuverability class C, flying at 48” without a rider, 36” carrying up to 210 pounds, and 24” carrying 211 to 350 pounds. It can be used at most 3 times per week, 12 hours per day. After 12 hours, or whenever the command word is spoken, it shrinks back to a statuette.

Golden lions: a pair that become 2 normal adult male lions (armor class 5/6, 5 + 2 hit dice, normal attacks). If slain in combat, they cannot be brought back from statuette form for 1 full week; otherwise they can be used once every day. They grow and shrink when the command word is spoken.

Ivory goats: a trio, each looking slightly different because each has a different function. After 3 uses each goat loses its magic forever.

  1. Goat of Travelling: a fast, tireless mount: armor class 6, 24 hit points, 2 horn attacks for 1-8 each (treat as a 4 hit dice monster). It moves 48” carrying 280 pounds or less, −1” for each extra 14 pounds. It can travel at most 1 day each week (continuously, or in any combination of periods totalling 24 hours). Then, or when the command word is spoken, it returns to small form for at least 1 day before it can be used again.
  2. Goat of Travail: becomes an enormous creature, bigger than a bull, with sharp hooves (4-10/4-10), a vicious bite (2-8) and a pair of exceptionally large, wicked horns (2-12/2-12). When charging it can only use its horns, but adds +6 to each hit that round (8-18 h.p. per horn). It is armor class 0, has 96 hit points, attacks as a 16 hit dice monster and moves 24”. It can be called to life only once per month.
  3. Goat of Terror: becomes a destrier-like mount: 36” movement, armor class 2, 48 hit points, and no attacks of its own. But its rider can use its horns as weapons: one as a +3 spear (lance), the other as a +6 sword. When ridden against an opponent it radiates terror in a 3” radius; any opponent there must save versus magic or lose 50% of strength and suffer at least −3 “to hit”, from the weakness of terror. When all opponents are slain, or on command, it returns to statuette form. It can be used once every 2 weeks.

Marble elephant: the largest figurines, each about the size of a human hand. On command it grows to the size and statistics of a real elephant, or shrinks back. It obeys its commander completely, serving as beast of burden, mount, or attacking alone. Roll for its type:

01-50 Asiatic (Elephant)
51-90 African (Loxodont)
91-93 Prehistoric (Mammoth)
94-00 Prehistoric (Mastodon)

Details of each are in the MM. It can be used for at most 24 hours at a time, 4 times per month.

Obsidian steed: a small, nearly shapeless lump of black stone; only careful inspection shows it vaguely resembles a four-legged animal, though it radiates magic if detected. On command it becomes a true nightmare that can be ridden, but if the rider is good, it is 10% likely each use to carry its “master” to the floor of the first layer of Hades and then turn back into a statuette. See MM for the nightmare. It can be used for up to 24 hours, once per week. When it becomes astral or ethereal, its rider and gear do too, so it makes travel to other planes easy.

Onyx dog: becomes a creature like a war dog, but with intelligence 8-10, able to speak the common tongue, and with exceptional senses. By scent it can follow the trail of a known creature 100% of the time if the trail is 1 hour old or less, −10% per hour after that, though false trails, breaks, water, and masking or blocking substances or scents can throw it off. It has 90’ infravision, and spots hidden things (such as in shadows) 80% of the time, normally invisible things 65%, and astral, ethereal and out-of-phase things 50%. For details see DOG, WAR in the MM. It can be used for up to 6 continuous hours, once per week, and obeys only its owner.

Serpentine owl: on command becomes a normal-sized horned owl (AC 7; 24” move; 2-4 hit points; attacks for 1-2/1-2 hit points), or a giant owl, though the giant form can be used only 3 times, after which the statuette loses all its magic. In normal size it moves with 95% silence, has 90’ infravision, and sees in normal above-ground darkness as if in full light, twice as well as a human. Its hearing can detect a mouse moving 60’ away, so silent movement chances against it are halved. It communicates telepathically with its owner, reporting everything it sees and hears as well as its (low, 2-4) intelligence allows. In giant size it is in every way a giant owl (see Owl, giant, in the MM). Like most other figurines, it readily obeys all its owner’s commands.

The wearer can swim as fast as a triton (15”) under water and as fast as a merman (18”) on the surface, though they do not allow breathing water. They also give a very strong grip for climbing vertical or nearly vertical surfaces, up or down, with a 95% chance of not slipping and falling, or 99.5% for a thief.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like nothing more than a rough, long-prismed gem. On the proper words it gives off light in 3 ways:

  • Pale light: a cone 10’ long, 2½’ in radius at the end. Uses no charges.
  • Bright ray: only 1’ across but 50’ long. A creature struck in the eyes is dazzled and unable to see for 1-4 rounds, unless it saves versus magic (to see whether it shut or turned its eyes in time). 1 charge.
  • Blinding flash: a cone 30’ long and 5’ in radius at the end, lasting only a moment. Every creature in it must save versus magic or be blinded for 1-4 rounds and then suffer −1 to −4 “to hit” from permanent eye damage. 5 charges.

Cure blindness removes dazzling or blindness; only heal cures the eye damage. The gem has 50 charges and cannot be recharged. A darkness spell drains 1 charge or makes it useless for 1 round, as the owner chooses; continual darkness makes it useless for 1 day or drains 5 charges, as the owner chooses.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 17,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A finely cut and polished stone, normally indistinguishable from an ordinary jewel, though detect magic reveals its dweomer. Looking through it reveals all hidden, illusory, invisible, astral, ethereal or out of phase things within viewing range. It is slow, tedious work: range is 30” for a quick scan looking only for large, obvious objects, or 10” to see small things; a quick scan of a 200’ square area takes 1 round, a careful look at a 100’ square area 2 rounds. Each time it is used there is a 5% chance the viewer sees a hallucination, sees something that is not there, or sees through something real as if it were an illusion.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A broad leather band that looks like an ordinary adventurer’s belt, but is magical. When buckled on, it immediately changes its wearer’s sex to the opposite one, and then, its curse fulfilled, loses all power. The original sex cannot be restored by normal means, though a wish might (50% chance), and a powerful being can change things; it takes a god-like creature to put things right with certainty. 10% of these girdles remove all sex from the wearer instead.

Experience points 200 · Sale value 2,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

When found, it looks like an ordinary iron or steel helmet (basinet, sallet, etc.). Worn, it works only when a special command word is spoken, and then its true nature is plain to all: +2 armor of brilliant silver and polished steel, set with 10 diamonds, 20 rubies, 30 fire opals and 40 opals, each large and magical. In bright light it sparkles, sending reflected rays in all directions from its crown-like, gem-set spikes.

The gems:

  • Diamond: prismatic spray (as the seventh level illusionist spell)
  • Ruby: wall of fire (as the fifth level druid spell)
  • Fire opal: fireball (as the third level magic-user spell)
  • Opal: light (as the first level cleric spell)

Each gem’s power takes only 1 segment, but each can be used only once, and the helm can be used once per round. Double the spell’s level to find the level it is cast at for range, duration and so on.

Other powers, while any gems still have magic:

  1. It glows bluish when undead are within 30’; the light pains them and does 1-6 points of damage to all except skeletons and zombies.
  2. The wearer can command any sword he or she wields to become a sword of flame (q.v.), in addition to any other special properties it has; this takes 1 round.
  3. The wearer can produce flame as a 5th level druid.
  4. The wearer is protected as if by a double strength fire resistance ring, which cannot be increased by further magic.

When all the gems have lost their magic, the helm loses all its powers and the gems turn to worthless powder. Removing a gem destroys it. They cannot be re-enchanted.

If the wearer fails a saving throw against a magical fire attack, he or she must make another for the helm, without magical bonuses. If this fails too, all the remaining gems overload and explode, producing all their normal effects at once.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 60,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

name: Helm of Comprehending Languages & Reading Magic

system.description:
Looks like a normal war helmet. The wearer understands 90% of strange tongues and writings, and 80% of magical writings. (These percentages decide whether all or none of a speech, writing or inscription is understood. Understanding does not necessarily mean being able to use a spell.) It also counts as a normal helmet of the kind that goes with armor class 5.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 12,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like a typical helmet and radiates an unclear dweomer if tested. As soon as it is put on, its curse takes effect and the wearer’s alignment changes radically: good to evil, neutral to some absolute commitment (LE, LG, CE, CG), as different from the old alignment as possible. The change is mental, and once made, the person wants it, and will make no attempt to return to the old alignment. Only a wish or alter reality can restore it. A paladin must undertake a special quest and atone to undo the curse. Once it has worked, the helm loses all its magic.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A sturdy metal helmet that looks normal, though it radiates magic if detected.

Reading thoughts: the wearer can read the thoughts of creatures within 6”, if he or she knows the language they think in (racial tongue in preference to common, common in preference to alignment languages), and there is no more than 3’ of solid stone, ¼’ of iron, or any solid sheet of lead or gold in between. It is directional and needs conscious effort.

Communicating: the wearer can talk with any creature in range that shares a language, or send emotions (empathy) so the creature receives the wearer’s emotional message.

Suggestion: the wearer can try to implant a suggestion (see the third level magic-user spell of that name under CHARACTER SPELLS in the PHB). The wearer is 5% more likely to succeed for every 2 points of intelligence above the target’s, and 5% less likely for every 1 point below; so the target saves versus magic at −1 for every 2 points of intelligence it has below the wearer’s, or +1 for every 1 point above; equal intelligence means no adjustment.

The helm gives +4 against psionic attacks (see ATTACK MATRICES) and adds 40 points to total psionic strength.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 35,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Another normal-looking helmet that gives off a magical aura if detected. Any wearer can teleport (q.v.) once per day exactly as a magic-user does (the destination must be known, and there is risk). A magic-user can use its full power: he or she memorizes a teleport spell, and the helm refreshes the memory, so the spell can be cast up to 3 times on objects or characters while still keeping the helm’s own personal teleport. As long as the magic-user keeps the teleport spell uncast, he or she can personally teleport up to 6 times before the spell is forgotten, and even then the helm’s use (above) remains.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 30,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like a normal helmet, though detection shows it is magical. It lets the wearer see and breathe underwater. Small lenses drawn across from compartments on each side let the wearer see 5 times farther than normal human vision allows in the water and light conditions (weeds, obstructions, etc. still block vision as usual). When the command word is spoken, it makes and keeps a globe of air around the wearer’s head until the word is spoken again, so the wearer can breathe freely.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like a normal trumpet but shows a dweomer if magic is detected. It can be played as a normal horn, but when the right word is spoken and it is blown properly:

  1. A cone of sound 12” long and 3” wide at the base comes out, and everyone in it must save versus magic. Those who save are stunned for 1 round and deafened for 2. Those who fail take 1-10 hit points of damage, are stunned for 2 rounds and deafened for 4.
  2. At the same time, a pulse of ultrasonic sound 1’ wide and 10” long weakens materials such as metal, stone and wood, as much as 3 times the damage of a hit from a large catapult missile: 18 structural points, enough to smash a drawbridge or flatten a normal cottage.

It has no charges, but if blown magically more than once per day, there is a 10% cumulative chance that it explodes, doing 5-50 hit points of damage to the one blowing it. Each magical use also gives a 2% cumulative chance that it shatters, though this does no damage to the player.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 55,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

rolls.label: Horn explodes (10% cumulative after the first use each day)

system.description:
Radiates magic if detected, and looks like a normal horn, or like any of the many magical ones. When blown it sounds a note and calls up a mass of bubbles that completely surround and blind the one who blew it for 2-20 rounds. But the bubbles only appear when a creature is actively trying to kill the character who blew it, so they may come very soon or after a very long time.

Experience points --- · Sale value --- gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like a normal musical instrument, perhaps a bugle or warning horn. If blown without first speaking the proper rune, or 10% of the time in any case:

  • Outside: 2-12 fist-sized rocks rain down on the player, each doing 1-6 hit points of damage.
  • Indoors: the ceiling overhead collapses, doing 3-36 hit points of damage.
  • Underground: the area right above the player falls on him or her, doing 5-20 hit points base, multiplied by 1 for each 10’ of height it falls (twice the damage for a 20’ ceiling, three times for 30’, etc.).

Proper use: pointed at the roof 30’ to 60’ beyond the user, it collapses a section up to 20’ wide and 20’ long (10’ radius around the aiming point), doing the damage above indoors or underground only.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A conch shell horn that can be blown only once per day, except by a triton, who can sound it 3 times daily. Blown properly, it does any 1 of these:

  1. Calms rough waters in a 1 mile radius (which also dispels a water elemental or water weird).
  2. Summons 5-20 hippocampi (1-2 on d6), 5-30 giant sea horses (3-5), or 1-10 sea lions (6), if the character is in a body of water where such creatures live. They are friendly and obey the character who blew it as well as they understand.
  3. Panics marine creatures of animal intelligence or lower, making them flee unless each saves versus magic; those who save suffer −5 “to hit” for 3-18 turns (30-180 rounds).

Every triton within 1 league hears any sounding of the horn.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 17,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Each of the 4 kinds summons a number of berserkers from Valhalla to fight for the character who blows it, once every 7 days. All look like normal instruments until their command word is found.

A character whose class cannot use a particular horn is attacked by the fighters he or she summons.

The fighters are armor class 4, have 6 hit points per die, and are armed with sword and spear (50%) or battle axe and spear (50%). They gladly fight whoever the horn’s owner commands, until they or their opponent(s) are slain, or 6 turns pass, whichever comes first.

Fully 50% of these horns are aligned and summon only fighters of the horn’s alignment; a radical alignment difference means the fighters attack the one who blew it.

4 normal-looking magical iron horseshoes that never wear out. Fixed to any horse’s hooves, they double its speed. There is a 1% chance per 7 leagues travelled that 1 falls off; if this goes unnoticed, the horse’s speed drops to 150% of normal. If 2 are lost, speed is normal.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Iron shoes fixed like normal horseshoes. The horse travels without actually touching the ground, so it can cross water and leaves no tracks on any ground. It moves at normal speed and does not tire for as long as 12 hours of continuous riding per day while wearing them.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 7,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Small rectangular blocks of sweet-smelling incense, indistinguishable from non-magical incense until lit. Any cleric of 5th or higher level recognizes its special fragrance and pearly smoke when it burns. If a cleric lights a block and spends 8 hours praying and meditating near it, he or she gains the fullest and best spell effects: cure wounds spells always heal the maximum, spells cover the widest area possible, saving throws against them are at −1, and when the dead are brought back to life, the cleric halves their chance of not surviving (rounded down). 2-8 pieces are found. One piece burns for 8 hours, and the effects last 24 hours.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 7,500 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks exactly like incense of meditation. If lit while the cleric meditates and prays nearby, its odor and smoke make the cleric totally sure that the incense has made his or her spells superior. The cleric is completely determined to use spells at every opportunity, usually when they are not needed or are useless, and stays obsessed until all spells are cast or 24 hours pass. There are normally 2-8 pieces, each burning for 1 hour.

system.description:
There are 7 of these magical instruments. Each can be fully used only by a bard, especially one of at least as high a college as the instrument is named for (Fochlucan, Mac-Fuirmidh, Doss, etc.). Lower bards, and other characters who can play, get only limited results.

Fochlucan Bandore: a small 3-stringed instrument. Played by a 1st level bard (probationer) or a non-bard, it has a 50% chance per round of casting faerie fire, but if it does there is a 10% chance the player is outlined instead of the intended target. A bard of Fochlucan or higher college casts faerie fire at base 50% per level above 1st, and the reverse effect drops by 1% per level above 1st. Played properly it can also: 1. add 10% to the bard’s charm percentage; 2. cast entangle once per day; 3. cast shillelagh once per day; 4. let the bard speak with animals once per day. A 1st level bard trying these has a 30% chance they work, but a 70% chance of taking 2-8 hit points of damage.

Mac-Fuirmidh Cittern: a lute-like instrument, 50% likely to do 3-12 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard under 5th level, who picks it up and tries to play. A bard of 5th or higher level gets 15% better chance of charming and can sing songs once per day that: 1. cast barkskin; 2. cure light wounds; 3. cast obscurement. Lower level bards cannot use it, whether or not they take damage.

Doss Lute: 60% likely to do 4-16 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard under 8th level, who tries it. A bard of 8th or higher level gets 20% better chance of charming and can sing magical songs once per day that: 1. cast hold animal; 2. neutralize poison; 3. cast protection from fire in a 10’ radius.

Canaith Mandolin: 70% likely to do 5-20 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard under 11th level, who plays it. A bard of 11th or higher level adds 25% to charming and can cast once per day: 1. cure serious wounds; 2. dispel magic; 3. protection from lightning in a 10’ radius.

Cli Lyre: 80% likely to do 6-24 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard below 14th level, who plays it. A bard of 14th or higher level adds 30% to charming and can cast, by singing and playing, once each per day: 1. control winds; 2. transmute rock to mud; 3. wall of fire.

Anstruth Harp: 90% likely to do 8-32 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard below 17th level, who tries to strum it. A bard of 17th or higher level adds 35% to charming and can cast one each per day: 1. cure critical wounds; 2. wall of thorns; 3. weather summoning.

Ollamh Harp: does 10-40 hit points of damage to any non-bard, or bard under 20th level, who plays it. A bard of 20th or higher level adds 40% to charming and can cast one each per day: 1. confusion; 2. control weather; 3. fire storm.

All bard instruments: powerful magic makes every one look exactly alike. Any character able to play one can sing to do each of these once per day, for as many turns as the college’s order (1-7, or 8 turns for a magnus alumni with any of the 7): 1. a 10’ radius protection from evil; 2. become invisible (the playing and singing can still be heard faintly, but the exact location cannot be found without detection of invisibility); 3. levitate; 4. fly. Each ability takes 5 segments to start and at least 1 full round to complete.

If the bard’s charm chance goes over 100% with the instrument’s bonus, creatures save against it at −1 for every 5% over 100%, rounding 3% or 4% up to the next 5% (3% = 5%, 8% = 10%, 13% = 15%, etc.). Roll for the instrument found:

1-5 Fochlucan Bandore
6-9 Mac-Fuirmidh Cittern
10-12 Doss Lute
13-15 Canaith Mandolin
16-17 Cli Lyre
18-19 Anstruth Harp
20 Ollamh Harp

Counts as a +2 magic weapon, though it has no bonus “to hit” or damage. Range is 9”. When it strikes, it becomes the head of a lightning stroke ½” wide and 3” long, running back from the point of impact 3” toward the thrower (draw a straight line). The creature hit takes 1-6 hit points of damage plus 20 hit points of electrical damage; other creatures in the path of the back stroke take 20 or 10 hit points. The javelin is used up in the discharge. 2-5 are found.

Experience points 250 · Sale value 3,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Not thrown: when a command word is spoken, it launches itself. Range is 6”, all counted as short range. It is +6 “to hit” and does 7-12 hit points of damage. It can fly horizontally, vertically or any combination, to the full extent of its range. Its magic is good for only 1 throw. 2-8 are found.

Experience points 250 · Sale value 3,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A gleaming gem that radiates magic and seems valuable, but it is cursed: wandering monsters are 100% more likely to be encountered, and when the party tries to escape encountered monsters by fleeing, pursuit is 100% more likely. Once picked up, it always magically returns to its finder (hiding itself in a pouch, bag, pack, pocket, etc.) until remove curse or atonement is cast on him or her.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Looks like a very fine stone of some kind, though detect magic reveals its dweomer. Placed with other gems, it doubles the chance (+100%) that each goes up in value, from 1 in 10 to 2 in 10. It has 10-100 facets, and each time a gem goes up in value because of it (a roll of 2 on d10), 1 facet disappears. When all are gone, it is a worthless spherical stone.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000/facet gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

A sovereign salve for drawing poison, curing disease or healing wounds. A jar is small (perhaps three inches across and one inch deep) but holds 5 applications. Put on a poisoned wound (or swallowed), it detoxifies any poison or disease. Rubbed on the body, it heals 9-12 points of damage. 1-3 jars are usually found.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E3, UA III.E.3

Contains much arcane knowledge for magic-users (including illusionists) of neutral alignment (neutral, chaotic neutral, lawful neutral). A character of that class and alignment who spends a full week cloistered and undisturbed pondering it gains enough experience points to be exactly at the mid-point of the next higher level. The libram then vanishes completely, and that character can never benefit from such a work again.

A non-neutral magic-user who reads even a line takes 5-20 points of damage, is unconscious for as many turns, and must have a cleric atone for him or her before gaining any more experience. A non-magic-user who reads it must save versus magic or go insane, needing remove curse and 1 month of rest, or a cleric’s heal, to recover.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Exactly like the Libram of Gainful Conjuration, except that it benefits evil magic-users, and non-evil magic-users lose 1 level of experience just from looking inside its brass-bound covers, as well as suffering the other ill effects of reading even 1 line.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

The reverse of the Libram of Ineffable Damnation: very beneficial to good magic-users, very harmful to non-good ones. Like all such magical works, it vanishes after 1 week of study, and the character who benefits can never be helped by it again.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Its enchantments make it look like a normal instrument, and even if its magic is detected, it cannot be told from an instrument of the bards until played.

  • Protection: once per day, the proper chords negate the effects of a horn of blasting, a disintegrate spell, or 6 rounds of an earth elemental’s attack, as far as constructions are concerned.
  • Building: once per week, it can be strummed to magically build buildings, mines, tunnels, ditches or whatever: 3 turns of playing equals the work of 100 men laboring for 3 days.

A false chord gives a 20% chance that all its effects are negated. Once the character knows the proper chords, a false chord is only 5% likely, rising to 50% if the player is disturbed by physical or mental attack.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 30,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Like all magical writings of this kind, this metal-bound book looks arcane and rare but non-magical, though detect magic shows an aura. Any single character who reads it (24 hours of reading over 3-5 days) learns how to raise his or her constitution by 1 point through a regimen of special diet and breathing exercises over 1 month. The point is gained only after the regimen is followed. The book disappears as soon as it is finished, and the knowledge is forgotten in 3 months; it cannot be told or recorded. The manual is useless to the same character a second time, and only one character can benefit from it.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Like the Manual of Bodily Health, but reading it and following its course of exercise adds 1 point to the reader’s strength.

A treatise on building and animating a golem, with all the information and incantations needed to make 1 of the 4 kinds (cf. 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, Golem). Building takes a long time and much money, during which a single magic-user or cleric must have the manual at hand to study and must not be interrupted. Roll for the kind found (C = cleric, M = magic-user):

When the golem is finished, the writing fades and the book burns up; sprinkling its ashes on the golem brings it fully to life. The user is assumed to be 10th level or higher; for each level below 10th, there is a cumulative 10% chance that the golem falls to pieces within 1 turn of being finished, because of the maker’s imperfect understanding.

A cleric who reads a magic-user’s manual loses 10,000-60,000 experience points; a magic-user who reads a cleric’s manual loses 1 level of experience. Any other class takes 6-36 hit points of damage just from opening it.
