name: Manual of Puissant Skill at Arms

system.description:
Expert advice and instruction on weapon use and various ways of attack and defense. Any single fighter (including a bard, but not a paladin or ranger) who reads it and practices its skills for 1 month advances to the mid-point of the next higher level. The book disappears once read, and the knowledge is forgotten within 3 months, so it must be acted on fairly quickly. The fighter cannot explain or record what was read. A paladin or ranger understands it but cannot benefit. A cleric (including druid), thief (including assassin) or monk who handles or reads it will not understand it. A magic-user (including illusionist) who so much as glances at a few of its letters is stunned for 1-6 turns and loses 10,000-60,000 experience points, since the work is so opposed to magic use. Only one reading can benefit the same character.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Its heavy covers and metal bindings make it look like any of scores of semi-valuable, non-magical books. It contains secret formulae and recipes for ointments and exercises. A single reader who studies it for 3 days without interruption and then faithfully practices the skills for 1 month gains 1 point of dexterity, but only after the month of training. The manual disappears right after reading; the contents are remembered for 3 months but cannot be explained or recorded. Reading another such text adds no more dexterity to the same character.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A guide to thievery so learned that any single thief who reads it and then practices its skills for 1 month gains enough experience points to be at the mid-point of the next higher level. The text disappears after reading; the knowledge lasts 3 months but, as with other such texts, cannot be recorded or told. Reading another such manual is of no further benefit to the same character.

  • Assassins gain only 5,000 experience points, after reading and pondering it for 1 week.
  • Fighters, magic-users and monks cannot understand it.
  • Clerics, rangers and paladins who read even a word take 5-20 hit points of damage and are stunned for as many rounds, and if they fail a saving throw versus magic they also lose 5,000-20,000 experience points. They must also atone within 1 day or lose 1 point of wisdom.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

rolls.label: Cleric, ranger or paladin reading (also rounds stunned)
Experience lost on a failed save (×1,000)

system.description:
A huge digging tool 10’ long, weighing over 100 pounds. Any giant-sized creature with strength 20 or more can use it to loosen (or topple) earth (or earthen ramparts) in a 100 cubic foot area in 1 turn, or smash rock in a 20 cubic foot area in the same time. As a weapon it is +3 “to hit” and does 5-30 hit points of damage, not counting strength bonuses. (Cf. girdle of giant strength.)

Experience points 3,500 · Sale value 7,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A huge mallet 8’ long, weighing over 150 pounds. Any giant-sized creature with strength 21 or more can use it to drive piles up to 2’ across into normal earth at 4’ per blow, 2 blows per round. It smashes to splinters an oak door up to 10’ high by 4’ wide by 2 inches thick in 1 blow (2 if the door is heavily bound with iron). As a weapon it is +2 “to hit” and does 10-40 hit points of damage, not counting strength bonuses.

Experience points 4,000 · Sale value 12,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks like a normal neck chain, usually of bronze, copper or nickel-silver, with a disc pendant. Concentrating for a full round, the wearer picks up thoughts in a path 1’ wide at the medallion, widening 2’ every 10’, to a maximum width of 11’ at 50’ (5”). It is blocked by stone over 3’ thick, metal over 1/6’ thick, or any continuous sheet of lead, gold or platinum thicker than paint. Check each time it is used: on a roll of 6 on d6 it malfunctions (no result).

Only surface thoughts of creatures in the path are picked up. Their general distance can be told, but thoughts are understood only if the user knows their language. Creatures that use no language give off only their main emotions, which can only be understood with an ESP-Empathy medallion (see below). Undead and mindless golems have no readable thoughts or emotions. (See also PSIONICS.) Roll for the type found:

1-15 30’ range
16-18 30’ range with empathy
19 60’ range
20 90’ range

Thoughts cannot be sent through any medallion of ESP.

Experience points 1,000/3,000 · Sale value 10,000/30,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Exactly like a medallion of ESP in every way, even its range. But as well as picking up creatures’ thoughts, it broadcasts the user’s thoughts to the creatures in the path, alerting them. It works correctly, without projecting thoughts, only on a roll of 6.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A crystal mirror, usually about 4 square feet, framed in metal, wood, etc. Only magic-users can use it, though it can be fixed to a surface and set to work on its own by a command word. It has 13 to 18 non-spatial, extra-dimensional compartments.

Any creature that comes within 30’ and sees its reflection in it must save versus magic or be trapped, bodily, in one of the cells. A creature unaware of what the mirror is will certainly (100%) see its reflection; one actively avoiding it, 50%; one that knows the mirror traps life, 20%. Size does not matter, but automatons and non-living matter (including golems, but not intelligent undead) are not trapped. If the mirror is full, 1 random victim is freed to make room for the newest. If the mirror is broken, all victims are freed (usually to attack its owner).

The owner can call the reflection of any trapped creature to the surface and talk with the powerless creature, and can free a trapped creature by speaking a command word, but must know which cell it is in. Example: “By the power of this mirror I command the occupant of the 3rd cell to come forth!”

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks like an ordinary mirror, typically 5’ × 2’. An owner who knows the proper commands can make it:

  1. read the thoughts of any creature reflected in it, even in an unknown language;
  2. scry like a crystal ball with clairaudience, even into other planes if the viewer knows enough about them;
  3. serve as a portal to other places (possibly other planes too, at the DM’s option): scry the place first, then step through. An invisible area stays on the “other side”, and users can return if they can find the right spot. (Creatures being scried can step through too if they find it!);
  4. once per week, answer one short question briefly about a creature whose image is shown in it.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks exactly like a normal mirror. Any creature reflected in it creates an exact duplicate of itself, which immediately attacks. The duplicate has all the original’s items and powers (including magic), but when either is defeated or destroyed, the duplicate and its items vanish completely.

Experience points --- · Sale value 2,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A chain that looks like a medallion. The wearer can ignore all gases that affect creatures through breathing, can breathe underwater, and can even survive in airless space for up to 7 days.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Special enchantments make it look like a cheap medallion or worthless jewelry, but a character who puts it on sees it as it really is: golden missile globes hanging from a golden chain. Only the wearer can detach the spheres, which can easily be thrown up to 7”, bursting at the end of their flight as magical fireballs. Roll for the number of missiles and their fireball damage in hit dice:

d20Missiles (hit dice of each)
1-4one 5-dice, two 3-dice
5-8one 6-dice, two 4-dice, two 2-dice
9-12one 7-dice, two 5-dice, four 3-dice
13-16one 8-dice, two 6-dice, two 4-dice, four 2-dice
17-18one 9-dice, two 7-dice, two 5-dice, two 3-dice
19one 10-dice, two 8-dice, two 6-dice, four 4-dice
20one 11-dice, two 9-dice, two 7-dice, two 5-dice, two 3-dice

For example, a roll of 9-12 gives 7 missiles: one 7-dice, two 5-dice and four 3-dice fireballs.

Their sizes show that the globes differ in power, but the dice and damage of each cannot generally be known. If the wearer or carrier fails a saving throw against a magical fire attack, the necklace must also save; if it fails, all remaining missiles explode at once.

Experience points 50* · Sale value 200* gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks like a normal, inexpensive piece of jewelry until put on, and even then its nature is revealed only if the wearer is a cleric (not a druid, nor others who can use cleric or druid spells, such as paladins and rangers). It has 25-30 semi-precious (60%) and fancy (40%) stones, and makes the wearer 25% more likely to successfully petition his or her deity for desired spells. There are also 3-6 special beads (precious stones, gems of 1,000 g.p. base value); roll for each:

d20Bead
1-5Atonement: as the 5th level spell of the same name
6-10Blessing: as the 1st level spell of the same name
11-15Curing: cures blindness, disease or serious wounds (as the appropriate spell)
16-17Karma: the cleric casts spells as if 4 levels higher (for range, duration, etc.)
18Summons: calls the cleric’s deity (90% probability) to come in material form (but it had better be for a good reason!)
19-20Wind walking: as the 7th level spell of the same name

Each special bead can be used once per day. If the cleric summons the deity for vain purposes, the deity takes the necklace as the least punishment. A bead’s function is known only when it is grasped and a commune spell is used. Special beads removed from the necklace lose all their powers.

Experience points 500** · Sale value 3,000** gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Its enchantments completely hide what it is, and it can only be discovered by putting it on. It immediately tightens and cannot be removed except by alter reality, limited wish or wish. The wearer takes 6 hit points of strangulation damage per round until dead, and it stays clasped until the character is a dry skeleton.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A magical rope net so strong that strength under 20 cannot break it, and it counts as AC –10 against blows meant to cut it. (Sawing with a dagger or sword will not work; it must be hacked to cut a strand.) Each net is 10’ square with ¼’ mesh.

  • It can be thrown 20’ to cover and close on opponents; each one in its area must save versus magic to avoid being caught.
  • It can be hung from a ceiling (or generally overhead) and dropped on a command word.
  • It can be laid on the floor and close upward on command, stretching to enclose up to a 5’ cube.

Its owner can loosen it on command.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 7,500 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks exactly like a net of entrapment, but works only underwater, where it can be commanded to shoot out up to 3” to trap a creature. Otherwise it is the same as that net.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 6,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Magical paints that let their owner create real objects just by painting them in 2 dimensions. They are applied with a stick tipped with bristles, hair or fur, and the paint flows out to form the object as the user concentrates on the image. Painting an object takes 1 turn.

One pot creates a 1,000 cubic foot object painted over a 100 square foot surface: a 10’ × 10’ × 10’ pit, a 10’ × 10’ × 10’ room, a large door with a passage behind it, etc. It must be painted on a surface (floor, wall, ceiling, door, etc.). Only normal, inanimate things can be made (doors, pits, flowers, trees, cells, etc.), not monsters, people, golems and the like. Valuable things (precious metals, gems, jewelry, ivory, etc.) look valuable but are really tin, lead, paste gems, brass, bone, etc. Normal armor or weapons can, of course, be made.

1-4 pots are found, usually with a single brush about 1’ long.

Experience points 500*** · Sale value 3,000*** gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks like a normal pearl of average size and color, but is a powerful aid to a magic-user: once a day it lets the owner recall any 1 spell, even one already cast, as long as it was among the spells he or she most recently memorized. Roll for its power:

01-25 first
26-45 second
46-60 third
61-75 fourth
76-85 fifth
86-92 sixth
93-96 seventh
97-98 eighth
99 ninth
00 recalls 2 spells of 1st to 6th level (use d6)

1 in 20 of these pearls has the opposite effect, making a spell be forgotten. Such a pearl can only be gotten rid of by exorcism or a wish!

Experience points 200**** · Sale value 2,000**** gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks like a normal pearl, but a cleric who keeps it for 1 month gains 1 point of wisdom at the end of the 30 days. After that the cleric must keep it on his or her person, or the point is lost. 1 in 20 are cursed and work in reverse; once the point of wisdom is lost, the pearl turns to powder, and the loss is permanent unless restored by magic such as a wish or a Tome of Understanding.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 5,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

An engraved gem enchanted to look like a gem of small value. Any character who claims it contracts a terrible rotting disease, a form of leprosy. It can only be removed by remove curse, then cure disease, then heal, limited wish or wish; or by crushing a periapt of health and sprinkling its dust on the victim. Otherwise, starting 1 week after claiming the item, the victim loses 1 point each of dexterity, constitution and charisma per week, and dies when any score reaches 0. Points lost to the disease are permanent even if it is later removed.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks exactly like a periapt of foul rotting, but its owner is immune to all diseases, except that of the foul rotting periapt, as long as he or she carries it.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Indistinguishable from the other periapts. Its owner gets a 10% chance per plus to save against poisons that normally allow no saving throw, a normal saving throw against poisons that are usually saved against at a penalty, and its plus added to all other saves against poison. Roll for its plus:

1-8 +1
9-14 +2
15-18 +3
19-20 +4

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 12,500 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Looks exactly like the other periapts. Its owner need never fear open, bleeding wounds, since it prevents them. It also doubles the normal rate of healing, or lets wounds heal normally that would not otherwise.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

There is no way to tell what it does until it is worn (normally, by a cleric). The wearer is aware of any action or item that would harm his or her alignment and standing with the deity before doing the action or becoming associated with the item, if he or she first takes a moment to consider it.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 7,500 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

Slows the aging of the cleric who wears it by one-quarter, even magical aging. A cleric who puts it on at age 20 ages 9 months every 12, so after 12 years he or she has aged only 9, and is physically 29 instead of 32. 1 in 20 are cursed to work in reverse.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

This arm wrapping seems beneficial, but it actually draws the attention of supernatural creatures of exactly the opposite alignment to the cleric wearing it, who is then plagued by powerful hostile creatures wherever such creatures are or can appear. A cleric of 10th or higher level draws the attention of his or her deity’s most powerful enemy, who interferes directly: a lawful good cleric attracts various demons, and eventually the notice of Orcus or Demogorgon. Once put on, it cannot be removed without an exorcism spell, and then a quest must be done to re-establish the cleric in his or her alignment.

Experience points --- · Sale value 2,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A set of wooden pipes that look ordinary, but an owner who learns the proper tune can call 10-60 (d6 × 10) giant rats (80%) or 30-180 (3d6 × 10) normal rats (20%), if either or both are within 40”. There is a 1 round delay for each 5” the rats must travel. The piper must keep playing until they arrive, and they are then 95% likely to obey as long as the piping continues. If the piper stops for any reason, the rats leave immediately. If called again, they are 70% likely to come and obey, 30% likely to turn on the piper. If the rats are controlled by a creature such as a vampire, the piper has a 30% chance per round of piping to take control; once control is taken, there is a 70% chance of keeping it if the other creature is actively trying to regain it.

Experience points 1,750 · Sale value 8,500 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A circle of magical cloth spun from phase spider webs woven with strands of ether and beams of Astral Plane luminaries. Fully opened it is 6’ across, but it folds as small as a pocket handkerchief. Spread on any surface, it creates an extra-dimensional hole 10’ deep. The hole can be “picked up” from inside or outside by taking the cloth’s edges and folding it; the entrance disappears, but anything inside stays. The only air inside is what was there when the space was created, so creatures that breathe cannot stay inside more than a turn or so without opening it again. The cloth gains no weight even if the hole is filled with gold, for example. Each portable hole opens on its own particular non-dimensional space.

Putting a bag of holding inside a portable hole tears a rift to the Astral Plane, and the bag and cloth are sucked into the void and lost forever. Putting a portable hole inside a bag of holding opens a gate to another plane, and the hole, the bag and any creatures within 10’ are drawn there, the hole and bag being destroyed.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

A small magical device of various forms, each meant for a special need and usable only once:

d20Token
1-4Anchor: moors a craft so it cannot move for 1 full day (or until the owner commands otherwise).
5-7Bird: drives off any kind of hostile flying creatures, or serves as transport equal in every way to a roc of the largest size (1 day duration).
8-10Fan: forms a huge flapping fan that can make a strong breeze (cf. THE ADVENTURE, WATERBORNE ADVENTURES) over an area large enough to drive one ship. This wind does not add to existing wind: it cannot turn a strong breeze into a gale, but can be used against it to make an area of relative calm or lighter winds (though not to change wave size in a storm, of course). It can be used up to eight hours a day, and does not work on land.
11-13Swan boat: forms a huge swan-like boat that swims at 24”, carrying 8 horses and gear or 32 men or any equal combination (duration 1 day).
14-18Tree: makes a great oak spring up: 6’ diameter trunk, 60’ height, 40’ top diameter.
19-20Whip: a huge leather whip appears and is wielded against any opponent desired (+1 weapon, 9th level fighter “to hit” probability, 2-7 hit points of damage plus save versus magic or be bound fast for 2-7 rounds) for up to 6 turns. (Cf. Dancing Sword.)

Other similar tokens may be added as desired.

TABLE (III.E.) 5.

Experience points 500/1,000 · Sale value 2,000/7,000 gp · DMG E4, UA III.E.4

rolls.label: Whip: bound fast on a failed save (rounds)

system.description:
A normal-looking garment that can be white (45%, good alignment), gray (30%, neutral, neither good nor evil) or black (25%, evil alignment). Its color cannot be known until a magic-user puts it on. Its wearer gains:

  1. armor equal to AC 5;
  2. 5% magic resistance;
  3. +1 on saving throws;
  4. when the wearer casts charm monster, charm person, friends, hold monster, hold person, polymorph other or suggestion, the targets’ magic resistance and/or saving throws are reduced by 20%/−4.

Wrong alignment: an evil wizard who puts on a white robe, or a good one a black robe, takes 18-51 (11d4 + 7) hit points of damage and loses 18,000-51,000 experience points. An evil or good magic-user putting on a gray robe, or a neutral one putting on a white or black robe, takes 6-24 hit points of damage and loses 6,000-24,000 experience points, and the robe’s enchantments push the wearer toward its alignment: the player should be urged aloud to change to the robe’s alignment, and the magic-user must work to keep the old alignment pure.

Experience points 6,000 · Sale value 65,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

An ordinary-looking robe that magic cannot detect. But the wearer senses a dweomer when putting it on and knows it is special. It makes the wearer seem part of a rock wall, a plant, a different kind of creature, whatever fits, with the right color, form and even smell, though it cannot make the wearer look more than twice or less than one-half normal height, and gives no ability to understand or imitate languages/noises. (Where several forms would fit, the wearer must say which one the robe should create.) Creatures who know and are friendly with the wearer see him or her normally.

Noticing something wrong (within 3” of the wearer): creatures of exceptional (15+) or better intelligence have a 1% chance per point of intelligence; creatures of low (5+) or better intelligence with 10 or more levels or hit dice have a 1% chance per level or hit die. These add together, so an 18 intelligence, 12th level magic-user has a 30% chance (18% + 12%). Check once for each eligible creature at first, then each turn the same creatures stay within 3”.

Experience points 3,500 · Sale value 35,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks like a normal robe until worn, but its scores of magical “eyes” let the wearer “see” in all directions at once. The wearer has 12” infravision, ultravision, and sees displaced or out of phase things and creatures where they really are. It sees all kinds of invisible things within 24” of normal vision (12” with infravision); invisibility, dust of disappearance, a robe of blending, even improved invisibility do not hide things from it, though solid objects still block its sight. It cannot see astral or ethereal things, illusions or secret doors, but easily spots creatures camouflaged or hiding in shadows, so the wearer cannot be ambushed or surprised. It also lets the wearer track as a 12th level ranger. A light spell cast directly on it blinds it for 1-3 rounds; continual light for 2-8 rounds.

Experience points 4,500 · Sale value 50,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks like some other kind of robe; detection reveals only a magic aura. As soon as a character puts it on, he or she drops to 3 intelligence, forgets all spells and magical knowledge, and becomes weak (3 strength) as well. It comes off easily, but restoring mind and body needs remove curse and then heal cast on the character.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks normal, though a magic aura can be detected. It works only for a wearer with intelligence 15 or higher and wisdom 13 or more, who can make it a shifting pattern of incredible colors, cascading from top to hem in sparkling, dazzling rainbows. It lights a 40’ diameter sphere, and also hypnotizes opponents so they cannot attack the wearer.

  • Starting the colors “flowing” takes a full round.
  • Each round they shift, any opponent who fails a save versus magic (after any magic resistance check) stands hypnotized for 2-5 rounds, and even when that wears off must save again to attack successfully.
  • Each round of continuous scintillation makes the wearer 5% harder to hit with missiles and hand-held or body weapons (hands, fists, claws, fangs, horns, etc.), up to 25% (−5) after 5 rounds.
  • After the first round, the wearer can cast spells or do anything that does not need moving more than 1” from where he or she started.

Outside combat, it simply hypnotizes creatures that fail their saves versus magic for 2-5 turns.

Experience points 2,750 · Sale value 25,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks like ordinary clothing, but a magic-user wearing it notices small cloth patches of various shapes sewn on it. Only the wearer can see, recognize and remove them, 1 per round, and each one removed becomes the real item. A robe always has 2 of each of these patches: dagger; pole (10’); lantern (filled and lit); rope (50’ coil); mirror (large); sack (large). It also has 4-16 of these, rolled for:

01-08 Bag of 100 gold pieces
09-15 Coffer (½’ × ½’ × 1’), silver (500 g.p. value)
16-22 Door, iron (up to 10’ wide and 10’ high and barred on 1 side, must be placed upright, will attach and hinge itself)
23-30 Gems, 10 of 100 gold piece value each
31-44 Ladder, wooden (24’ long)
45-51 Mule (with saddle bags)
52-59 Pit (10 cubic feet), open
60-68 Potion of extra healing
69-75 Rowboat (12’ long)
76-83 Scroll of 1 spell
84-90 War dogs, pair
91-96 Window (2’ × 4’, up to 2’ deep)
97-00 Roll twice more

Several items of the same kind are allowed. A removed item can never be replaced.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 15,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

A 60’ rope no thicker than a slender wand and weighing no more than 3 pounds, yet strong enough to hold 3,000 pounds. On command it snakes forward, up, down or any other direction at 10’ per round and fastens itself securely wherever wanted, and comes back or unfastens the same way; one end must be held by a character while it does so. It can also be told to knot itself, making large knots every 1’ along its length, which shortens it to 50’ while knotted.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks exactly like a rope of climbing or entanglement, but as soon as it is told to do anything, it whips around the neck of the character holding it and of 1-4 others within 10’ (each gets a saving throw versus magic), and strangles and crushes the life out of each victim, doing 2-12 hit points of damage per round until dispel magic is cast on it. A creature caught by it cannot cast spells or free itself by any means. It is AC −2 and takes 22 hit points to cut through; all the damage must be done by the same creature (not one that is caught).

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks exactly like any other magical rope. On command it lashes out 20’ forward, or 10’ upward, to entangle and tie fast up to 8 man-sized creatures. (Count 1 storm giant or fire giant = 2 frost or stone or hill giants = 3 ogres = 4 bugbears = 6 gnolls = 8 men = 10 elves = 12 dwarves = 16 gnomes or kobolds.) The command takes 1 segment, striking 1 more, and entwining another, 3 segments in all.

It cannot be broken by strength alone; it must be hit with an edged weapon. It is AC −2 and takes 22 hit points to cut through, all done by the same creature (not the one entangled). Damage under 22 hit points repairs itself in 6 turns. If it is cut through, it is destroyed.

Any magical rope that is broken or cut immediately loses its special properties.

Experience points 1,250 · Sale value 12,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

A finely woven carpet that looks like a carpet of flying and gives off magic if detected. But a character who sits on it and gives a command is in for a surprise: it rolls itself tightly around him or her and suffocates the victim in 3-6 rounds. It cannot be physically stopped from wrapping itself, and only alter reality, animate object, hold plant or wish can stop it smothering its victim.

Experience points --- · Sale value 1,500 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Looks exactly like a carpet of flying and works as one (6’ × 9’ size), but has other powers too:

  • On command it acts as a rug of smothering, trapping any creature up to ogre-size that steps on it.
  • It can stretch and stiffen to become as hard and strong as steel, up to 27’ long and 2’ wide, to serve as a bridge, barricade, etc. In this form it is AC 0 and takes 100 hit points to destroy.
  • Best of all, on a command word it shrinks to 1/12 size for easy storage and carrying.

Experience points 6,500 · Sale value 45,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

A notched adamantite blade 12’ long and over 1’ wide. One person needs 18/00 or greater strength to work it alone, or 2 people of 17 or greater strength can work it together. It cuts through a 2’ thick hardwood tree in 1 turn, a 4’ thick trunk in 3 turns, or a 1’ diameter tree in only 3 rounds. After 6 turns of sawing, the user(s) must rest for 6 turns before working again.

Experience points 1,750 · Sale value 12,500 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

A small magical brooch or pin that looks like one of the various helpful amulets, brooches or scarabs. But if it is held for more than 1 round, or kept in a container (bag, pack, etc.) within 1’ of a warm living body for 1 turn, it becomes a horrible burrowing beetle-like creature that tears through leather or cloth, burrows into flesh and reaches the victim’s heart in a single round, killing him or her. It then turns back into a scarab. (Kept in a container of hard wood, ceramic, bone, ivory or metal, it cannot come to life.)

Experience points --- · Sale value 2,500 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

When it is shown and a command spoken, all intelligent hostile creatures within 4” must save versus magic or fly into a berserk fury for 7-12 rounds, attacking the nearest creature (even their own comrades) at +1 “to hit” and +2 damage, but at 3 worse armor class. They attack constantly without reason or fear, moving on to the next nearest creature when their first opponent is slain. Those who save act normally. It has 19-24 charges.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 8,000 gp · DMG E5, UA III.E.5

Absolutely indistinguishable from any other amulet, brooch or scarab. When it is shown and a command word spoken, all other creatures within 2” must save versus magic at −2 (and with −10% to any magic resistance). How magic armor works: the DM must know the armor class system well. Earlier forms of the game worked upward from a high base number (9), and the same progression is kept here for continuity and familiarity. A shield is the one common factor, so it counts as +1, 1 class (5%) better than no armor, and is listed before the various armor types so it can be included as a constant (without over-valuing it). Each +1 of armor, of any type, moves the wearer one class better (toward or beyond AC 2 to 1, 0, −1, −2, etc.). So chain mail +1 is chain mail (AC 5) one class better (AC 4), while a shield +1 equals armor class 8, or 2 places better than the armor worn, rather than just 1 (+1 for carrying a shield, +1 for its magical bonus).

For game purposes all magical armor is virtually weightless, about like normal clothing, so wearers have the base movement of an unarmored man. Magic shields, however, weigh the same as normal shields of the same size. Armor of +3 bonus is made of special meteorite iron steel, +4 of mithral alloyed steel, +5 of adamantite alloyed steel.

Special items are described below:

Size: DMG says 65% of armor is man-sized, 20% elf-sized, 10% dwarf-sized and 5% gnome or halfling sized.

Note on armor types: a DM unfamiliar with medieval armor might find Charles ffoulkes’ ARMOUR AND WEAPONS (Oxford 1909) a short, useful book. The armor types here are fitted into a game system, and cover the following: LEATHER ARMOR is cuir bouli: coat, leggings, boots and gauntlets. STUDDED LEATHER adds protective plates set in the leather and an extra layer at the shoulders. RING MAIL is leather armor sewn with closely set iron rings. SCALE MAIL is a leather suit set with small overlapping iron plates. CHAIN MAIL needs no explanation. BANDED MAIL is horizontal strips of jointed armor plates worn over chain mail. SPLINT MAIL is a coat of vertical armor plates sandwiched in the layers of the garment, worn over chain. PLATE MAIL is a set of plate pieces (shoulder, breast, back, elbow, groin/hips, legs) worn over chain mail. Plate armor, a late development, is not included: the full suit of solid plate used c. 1500 is not a game armor type, though it was lighter and more mobile than plate mail! It was also two or three times more costly . . .

How magic armor works: the DM must know the armor class system well. Earlier forms of the game worked upward from a high base number (9), and the same progression is kept here for continuity and familiarity. A shield is the one common factor, so it counts as +1, 1 class (5%) better than no armor, and is listed before the various armor types so it can be included as a constant (without over-valuing it). Each +1 of armor, of any type, moves the wearer one class better (toward or beyond AC 2 to 1, 0, −1, −2, etc.). So chain mail +1 is chain mail (AC 5) one class better (AC 4), while a shield +1 equals armor class 8, or 2 places better than the armor worn, rather than just 1 (+1 for carrying a shield, +1 for its magical bonus).

For game purposes all magical armor is virtually weightless, about like normal clothing, so wearers have the base movement of an unarmored man. Magic shields, however, weigh the same as normal shields of the same size. Armor of +3 bonus is made of special meteorite iron steel, +4 of mithral alloyed steel, +5 of adamantite alloyed steel.

All magic swords get their stated bonus both to hit (added to the “to hit” die) and to damage (+1, +2, +3, etc. added to the hit points of damage). The special features of the listed swords are described below. After that come the unusual aspects swords may have (intelligence, abilities, powers, purpose, alignment, languages and ego), and finally the effects of unusual swords. Few swords have any unusual aspects.

All +5 Holy Avenger swords are lawful good. All Swords of Sharpness are chaotic. All Vorpal Weapons are lawful.

Most magic swords (and all magic daggers) shed light when drawn from their scabbards (see 1e Fantasy RPG, PHB, THE ADVENTURE, Light). The only exceptions are the Flame Tongue, Frost Brand, Holy Avenger, Life Stealing and Sharpness swords, which are dealt with individually.

Whenever a sword has some unknown quality, such as the wishes in a Luck Blade or unusual aspects, the DM should prepare a special 3 × 5 index card for it and keep it handy whenever its owner is playing.

The tables make most magic swords long swords (DMG: 70% long, 20% broad, 5% short, 4% bastard, 1% two-handed; UA: 65% long, 20% broad, 5% falchion, 5% short, 4% bastard, 1% two-handed). Change the base weapon if another type is rolled.

  • 2 charges: 2-12 points.
  • 3 charges (the maximum): 3-18 points.

The blow is strong. If the target fails a save versus spell, it is knocked free or knocked down, which makes the ring useful for knocking opponents off walls or ladders, or over ledges. The target applies these adjustments to its save:

ConditionAdjustment
Smaller than man-sized−1
Larger than man-sized+2
Strength under 12−1
Strength of 18-20+3
Strength over 20+6
4 or more legs+4
Over 1,000 lbs. weight+2
2 charges expended−1
3 charges expended−2

The DM should adjust for circumstances as needed, using common sense. For instance, a fire giant balanced on a narrow ledge should get no benefit from strength and weight unless he knows the blow is coming.

Opening doors: the ring can also open doors as if a person of 18/00 strength were doing it; with 2 charges, as strength 19; with 3 charges, as strength 20. Magically held or locked portals can be opened this way.

  • Structural damage: used this way, the force does the same structural damage as a real battering ram (see the DMG), doubled for 2 charges and tripled for 3 charges.
  • Items: magic items struck by the force must save versus crushing blow only if 3 charges are used; otherwise they are unaffected. Non-magical items targeted by the force must always save versus crushing blow.

Recharging: a magic-user can recharge it using enchant an item and clenched fist together. The first ring of this sort was made by the renowned magic-user Lythargyrhum.

Experience points 750 · Sale value 7,500 gp · UA III.C.2

This ordinary-looking ring gives off only a faint magic aura that cannot be identified, but it holds strong magic for harming an opponent. If the wearer tries to touch an enemy with the hand wearing the ring and makes a successful to-hit roll, the touch delivers 7-14 points of damage (d8 + 6). After three such discharges, however much time has passed between them, the ring is inert for 1 turn. While working, the ring makes a round, charged bump appear on the palm of the wearer’s hand.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 5,000 gp · UA III.C.2

This ring keeps its wearer nourished even if he or she goes for days without food or drink. It also refreshes body and mind, so the wearer needs only two hours of sleep per day to get the benefit of eight hours.

  • Attunement: it must be worn for a full week before it works. If removed, it loses its benefits at once and must be worn another week to attune again.
  • Rest period: after working (in either or both ways) for any seven consecutive days, it stops working for a week while its magic renews.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 3,500 gp · UA III.C.2

This ring is a mixed blessing. The wearer can tell when any lie is told to him or her, but cannot tell any sort of falsehood: every attempt to lie comes out as the literal truth. In return, the wearer can detect the last lie told by someone else; in fact, the liar’s voice rises to a falsetto because of the ring.

If the wearer meets magic that lets someone lie without being detected (for example, a person under an undetectable lie spell or a philter of glibness), no lie is noticed, but the wearer cannot hear that person’s voice at all, whether or not he or she is trying to listen.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 5,000 gp · UA III.C.2

This rod cannot be told apart from a footman’s mace +1 until it is used and its true powers show. Its powers are:

  • Always active: +1 to the possessor’s die rolls for being surprised, and +1 on initiative rolls in combat.
  • Detection: while grasping it firmly and concentrating, the possessor can detect alignment, evil, good, illusion, invisibility, lie, or magic. These detections cost no charges.
  • Alarm: if the rod is planted in the ground and the possessor wills it to alertness, it senses any creature within a 12˝ radius that intends harm to the possessor. When it does, each of the eight flanges on its mace head casts a light spell in one direction of the compass (N, NE, E, etc.) at 6˝ range; at the same time it places a prayer effect on all creatures friendly to the possessor within a 2˝ radius. Right after that, it sends a mental warning to those same friendly creatures about possible danger from the hostile creature(s) within the 12˝ radius.
  • Animate guardians: it can imitate an animate object spell on up to 16 objects the possessor has specially chosen and placed roughly around the edge of a 6˝-radius circle centered on the rod (16 chosen shrubs, 16 specially shaped branches, or the like).

Charges: the protective functions other than the animation cost 1 charge, and the animation costs 1 charge, so using all the rod’s protective powers at once costs 2 charges. A cleric of 16th or higher level can recharge it, provided at least 1 charge remains when recharging is tried.

Experience points 7,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · UA III.D

This weapon gives off a faint alteration aura when magic is detected. On its possessor’s command it changes from an ordinary-seeming rod into a double-headed flail. Changing it into a weapon, or back into a rod, costs no charges.

  • Form: in close quarters, or when the wielder is mounted, it is the small horseman’s flail; otherwise it is a footman’s flail. Base damage is 2-5/2-5 (S-M/L) or 2-7/2-8 (S-M/L) respectively.
  • Bonus: in either form it is +3 to hit and damage.
  • Two heads: each head is rolled for separately when the possessor attacks, so double hits are possible, either on one opponent or on two opponents of man-size or smaller standing side by side.
  • Protection: by spending 1 charge, the holder gains +4 to protection and +4 on saving throws for 1 turn. The rod does not need to be in weapon form for this.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.D

rolls.label: Damage per head
rolls.note: Includes the +3 bonus; each head is checked.

system.description:
This highly magical rod lets its wielder use these powers: astral travel, dimension door, passwall, phase door, and teleport without error, one at a time, one per round. It gives off an alteration-evocation aura.

  • Activation: spending 1 charge activates the rod, and the possessor can then use each of the five powers once. The rod stays charged for one day, or until all five powers have been used. No power can be used a second time until another charge is spent, which makes all five available again.
  • Group astral travel: the wielder may use astral travel on up to five willing creatures (the wielder must be one of them). Doing so cancels any other powers left from that activation. The rod goes into the Astral Plane with them and cannot be used or reactivated until it is brought back. This group use works only for astral travel, not for the other powers (such as passwall); astral travel is the only power that can affect more than one creature per activation, and only in this way.
  • Recharging: because the travelers’ physical bodies and possessions actually become astral, recharging the rod requires a magic-user of 20th or higher level.

Experience points 5,000 · Sale value 50,000 gp · UA III.D

Each charge spent creates a non-dimensional space, a “pocket paradise,” where the possessor and up to 199 other creatures can stay in complete safety.

  • Length of stay: at most 200 days divided by the number of creatures, with fractions rounded down. One creature (the possessor alone) can stay 200 days; four creatures, 50 days; 60 creatures, 3 days; any group of 101 to 200 creatures, only one day.
  • Conditions: those inside do not age (except from magical causes such as a wish), and natural healing and curing happen at twice the normal rate. Fresh water and food (fruits and vegetables only) are plentiful, and the climate is comfortable for everyone, so no protection from the elements is needed.
  • Going in: activating the rod instantly removes the wielder and every creature touched with the rod to the paradise. Members of a large group can hold hands or otherwise touch each other so all are “touched” by the rod at once.
  • Coming back: when the magic is cancelled or runs out, everyone instantly reappears where they were when the rod was activated. If something else now occupies a returning traveler’s space, his or her body is moved aside just far enough to make room.
  • Recharging: requires a cleric of 16th or higher level and a magic-user of 18th or higher level working together.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 30,000 gp · UA III.D

Constant powers: while the rod is held or carried, its possessor has a charisma of 18, and whatever he or she wears (armor included) looks to be of the finest quality and condition, though this gives no magical benefit such as a better armor class. If the possessor’s charisma is already 18 or more, the rod does not raise it further.

Noble garments (1 charge): the rod creates and dresses the possessor in noble clothing of the finest fabrics, adorned with furs and jewels.

  • The apparel is truly created and lasts permanently, unless the possessor tries to sell any part of it or any of it is taken from him or her by force. In either case all of it vanishes at once.
  • It may be given freely to other characters or creatures and stays whole and sound afterward.
  • While the possessor wears one of these outfits, spending another charge cannot replace or add to it; the charge is simply wasted.
  • Value of an outfit: 7,000 to 10,000 gp (d4 + 6). The fabric is worth 1,000 gp, furs 5,000 gp, and jewel trim 1,000 to 4,000 gp (for example, 10 gems of 100 gp each, 10 gems of 200 gp each, or 20 gems of 100 gp each, and so forth).

Palatial tent (1 charge): the rod creates a huge silk pavilion covering 1,500 to 3,000 square feet, with temporary furnishings and food fitting its splendor, enough to entertain up to 100 people. It lasts one day. At the end of that day another charge can be spent to keep it; otherwise the tent and everything connected with it (including anything taken out of it) disappears.

This rod cannot be recharged.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 25,000 gp · UA III.D

This clerical weapon looks like an ordinary wooden walking staff of the kind used for trekking in the wilderness, and gives off a very faint alteration aura. It is usually made of bronzewood, reinforced with heavy iron bands and tips. On command it takes whichever of these three forms its possessor wants:

  • Quarterstaff: quarterstaff +3, iron-shod.
  • Great Mace: footman’s mace +1, iron.
  • Mace: horseman’s mace +2, iron.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 12,500 gp · UA III.D

This quarterstaff seems to be only a +1 weapon unless a druid grasps it, which reveals its slinging power. Only a druid can use that power.

Slinging: the druid touches one end of the staff to a heavy, roughly round object (a stone, metal ball, pottery crock, etc.) up to nine inches across and five pounds in weight. The object sticks to the staff, and the druid releases it at a target with an overhand swing; it leaves the staff on the down-stroke.

  • Trajectory: normally low and rising, climbing 1 foot for every 1˝ traveled. The arc may be higher, or the missile may be aimed almost straight up; in that case reverse the ratio, so it covers 1 foot sideways for every 1˝ of rise.
  • Range: maximum 18˝; short range up to 6˝, medium up to 12˝.

Giant’s throw (1 charge): the druid can hurl a large missile as if he or she were a stone giant, to a range of 30˝, doing 3-30 points of damage per hit.

Whether used as a quarterstaff or with either slinging power, the staff gives +1 to hit and +1 per die of damage. A druid of 12th or higher level can recharge it.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · UA III.D

rolls.label: Giant-sized missile
rolls.note: +1 per die is added for the staff.

system.description:
This seemingly ordinary quarterstaff shows an alteration aura when examined magically. It responds to three commands:

  1. A long, sharp spear blade shoots out of its upper end, making it a spear instead of a staff.
  2. The weapon lengthens to a full 12 feet.
  3. It returns to its original form as a plain staff.

Each staff-spear’s power and value are rolled randomly the first time it is used:

Die rollTo hit & damageX.P. valueG.P. sale value
1-6+11,0005,000
7-10+21,5007,500
11-13+32,00010,000
14-16+42,50015,000
17-19+53,00020,000
20+3*3,50025,000

* Does damage as a ranseur (2-8), but still acts as a spear when used to thrust or when set to receive a charge.

Experience points 1,000-3,500 · Sale value 5,000-25,000 gp · UA III.D

This staff is usually rather short and very stout. When found, much of its length is covered in fine carvings of all kinds of winged biting and stinging insects (bees, deerflies, horseflies, wasps, and the like).

Swarm (1 charge): any cleric-type character (cleric, druid, shaman, witch doctor, etc.) holding the staff can command it to create a swarm of such insects.

  • Range: 6˝ + 1˝ per clerical level of the user.
  • Number: 60 insects plus 10 per level.
  • Damage: every 10 insects do 1 point of damage to the target, regardless of armor class, unless the target is protected by a force field, engulfed in flames, etc. The insects do not affect creatures larger than man-sized that have a natural armor class of 5 or better.
  • Effect on the target: a vulnerable creature attacked by the swarm can do nothing except try to brush off or kill the insects.
  • Duration: the attack lasts 1 round.

Charges: each use makes one of the carved insects vanish from the staff, so the remaining charges are easy to count. Unlike other staves, it can start with as many as 50 charges, but it cannot be recharged.

Experience points 100/chg. · Sale value 500/chg. gp · UA III.D

Even a casual look shows this stout quarterstaff is exceptional, and magical examination reveals an alteration aura. It is made of very stout wood (ash, oak, bronzewood, or the like), bound with iron and set with silver rivets. Without spending any charges, it is a +2 magic weapon. Its other powers:

  • Thunder (1 charge): the staff strikes as a +3 weapon. Unless the opponent struck saves versus rods, staves, and wands, the noise of the impact stuns it: it can take no further action in the round it was struck and automatically has last initiative in the next round.
  • Lightning (1 charge): a short spark leaps out when the opponent is struck, doing 2-12 points of shock damage in addition to the staff’s damage (compare wand of lightning). Even if the staff itself does not score a hit, the discharge ignores any metal armor (treat the target as AC 10 for this purpose), so the shock damage alone might apply.
  • Thunderclap (2 charges): the staff sends out a cone of deafening noise, ½˝ wide at the apex, 4˝ long, and 2˝ wide at its far end. Every creature wholly or partly in the cone must save versus rods, staves, and wands. Those who fail are stunned for 1-2 rounds (unable to attack) and then cannot hear for 1-2 more rounds. Those who save cannot hear for 1-4 rounds but lose no attacks.
  • Lightning stroke (2 charges): a bolt like that of a wand of lightning, but of eight dice (8d6), with rolls of 1 counted as 2, for 16-48 points of damage to those who fail a saving throw. The stroke may be single or forked.
  • Thunder & lightning (4 charges): combines the thunderclap above with a forked lightning bolt like the lightning stroke. The lightning does 8d6 with rolls of 1 or 2 counted as 3, for 24-48 points. Those who make the saving throw are only deafened and take half damage.

Activation time: any function takes as many segments as the charges it uses; for example, thunder & lightning costs 4 charges and takes 4 segments.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.D

rolls.label: Thunder and lightning (1s and 2s count as 3s)

system.description:
This staff is always made of finely grained oak, ash, or yew, beautifully carved and bound and shod with bronze. It works only for a druid.

Charged powers (one charge per use):

  • Wall of thorns.
  • Animal friendship and speak with animals.
  • Animate tree: like a treant’s ability, this makes a large tree move at a 3˝ rate and attack as if it were a treant of the largest size; in every other way it becomes a virtual treant for eight rounds per charge spent. The tree takes one round to animate and returns to rooting on the eighth, so only six of the first eight rounds can actually be used for attacking.

Weapon value and extra powers: each staff is also a magic weapon. Those with a lower bonus have extra powers that need no charges and can each be used once per day. Each of the four types is equally likely:

  • +4: no extra powers.
  • +3: pass without trace.
  • +2: pass without trace and barkskin.
  • +1: the powers of the +2 staff plus tree.

Experience points 8,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · UA III.D

This wand works like an ordinary wand of wonder, but it has no more than 50 uses before it is fully spent. It also has three special uses: on command, it can act as any other known kind of wand, but it can copy each kind of wand only once. If ordered to copy the same kind of wand a second or third time, the command has no effect, and after three such commands, whether they worked or not, the wand is completely drained and useless. It cannot be recharged.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 12,500 gp · UA III.D.2

A short, thick wand about 1½ feet long, with a very sharp point at one end and a trigger built into the other, blunt end. Any character except a cleric can use it, and it activates in a single segment.

When the thick end is grasped firmly and the trigger pressed, the tip becomes the equal of a dagger +1 and the rest of the shaft opens into a buckler-sized round shield with a +1 magic value. Together they form a spiked buckler +1.

  • Magic-users: because of its magic, magic-users can use it, but they cannot cast spells while it is in buckler form unless the possessor is multi-classed with fighter abilities as well as magic-user abilities.
  • Thieves: a thief using it cannot climb walls or use other abilities that need the hands while holding it.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 5,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This wand is never made of wood; it is usually made mostly of ivory or bone. Its functions:

  • 1 charge: all chlorophyll within a 3˝ radius of the wand is destroyed. Leaves turn autumn colors and fall, grass turns brown and dry, and so forth.
  • 2 charges: all normal plant life within the 3˝ radius withers and dies. Sentient plant creatures and other non-normal plants are not necessarily killed, but each takes 1-6 (1d6) points of damage.
  • 2 charges, as a cone: the possessor may instead direct the power into a cone 3˝ long that widens to 1˝ across at its far end. The effect is the same, except that sentient and non-normal plant life in the cone takes 6-36 points (6d6) instead of 1-6. A plant creature or other non-normal plant that is only partly inside the cone may save versus rods, staves, and wands; if it succeeds, it takes half damage (3d6).

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 6,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This wand is usually fairly short and tipped with some kind of mineral. Its powers:

  • Dig: ½ charge per use.
  • Passwall: 1 charge per use.
  • Move earth: 2 charges per use.

In addition, 50% of these wands (the higher-valued ones) also have:

  • Transmute mud to rock: 1 charge per use.
  • Transmute rock to mud: 1 charge per use.

Experience points 1,000-1,500 · Sale value 10,000-15,000 gp · UA III.D.2

The wielder can cast a fireball as if he or she were a 6th-level magic-user. The wand takes only 1 segment to activate and 1 segment to release the fireball. Damage is 6-36 points (6d6), with a saving throw for half damage. Any magic-user of 8th or higher level can recharge it.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 16,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This wand has three separate functions:

  • Normal fires (no charge): fires of normal sort and size are put out without using a charge. Normal size means anything up to a bonfire or a fire in an ordinary fireplace, about four to six logs burning hotly.
  • Large or minor magical fires (1 charge): large normal fires, flaming oil of a gallon or more, fire produced by a demon or devil, a flame tongue sword, or a burning hands spell. Continual magic flames, such as those of a sword or of a creature able to ignite, are put out for 6 rounds and then flare up again.
  • Large magical fires (2 charges): such as a fireball, flame strike, or wall of fire.
  • Creatures of flame (1 charge): used on a creature made of flame (a fire elemental, for instance), the wand does 6-36 (6d6) points of damage to it.

Experience points 1,250 · Sale value 10,000 gp · UA III.D.2

The idea of such a wand is said to have taken many forms, but the standard version has three functions. Only the third needs much skill from its user.

  1. Energy blade (1 charge per turn): a shaft of nearly invisible blue-white energy springs 4 feet out from the tip. It hits and does damage as a +5 bastard sword.
  2. Wall of force (1 charge per wall): copies the 5th-level magic-user spell wall of force as if cast by a 10th-level magic-user. Only one can be created per round.
  3. Forceful hand (½ charge per round): creates a nearly invisible plane of energy that acts as a forceful hand spell. Only a magic-user can use this function, and whatever his or her level, one of the hand/fist spells must be recorded in his or her spell books for study (not necessarily castable).

Fighters of all types can use the first and second functions.

Recharging: a magic-user of 16th or higher level can recharge it. The wand can also regain a single charge by touching a manifestation of any hand/fist spell, of a arcane sword spell, or of a wall of force. The touch acts as a disintegrate spell, instantly destroying the spell or manifestation, and the wand absorbs power equal to one charge.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 30,000 gp · UA III.D.2

The wielder can create an ice storm as if he or she were a 7th-level magic-user, either damaging hail or sleet with slippery conditions (see the ice storm spell). Activation takes 1 segment, and releasing the magic from the wand takes another 1 segment. A magic-user of 9th or higher level can recharge it.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.D.2

The possessor can cast a lightning bolt as if he or she were a 6th-level magic-user, either forked or single stroke. Damage is 6-36 (6d6) points, with a saving throw for half damage. The wand takes 1 segment to activate and another 1 segment to discharge the bolt. A magic-user of 8th or higher level can recharge it.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 16,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This wand seems to be nothing more useful than a wand of metal and mineral detection, but in the hands of a dwarf or gnome its special powers work:

  • 1 charge: transmute gold to lead, or lead to gold. Range 3˝; 1 to 6 pounds of metal (10 to 60 gp weight) is changed.
  • 2 charges: heat metal, as the druid spell. Range 3˝; it affects a single target area 3 feet across, heating up to 600 gp weight of metal within it.
  • 3 charges: cast any one of crystalbrittle, glassee, or glassteel as if the user were an 18th-level magic-user.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 10,000 gp · UA III.D.2

The wielder can make any single creature, of almost any size, grow or shrink by 50%. Its relative strength and power increase or decrease in proportion, provided the weapons it uses are in proportion too (or usable). An enlarged humanoid’s strength is roughly that of a giant of matching size: for example, 9 feet tall equals a hill giant and 19 strength; 13 feet tall equals a fire giant and 22 strength.

  • Range: 1˝.
  • Saving throw: the target and everything it wears or carries is affected unless it makes a saving throw. A willing target need not save.
  • Ending the effect: a dispel magic removes it, but the target must then make a system shock roll. The wand’s possessor can also will the effect to end before its duration runs out. The book gives no duration for the effect, so how long it lasts is Unknown and is left to the DM.
  • Charges: each use costs 1 charge; cancelling an effect costs none. A magic-user of 12th or higher level can recharge it.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This wand has two functions, each costing 1 charge:

  • Steam: in one segment the wand shoots out a jet of superheated steam in a cone 1˝ × 3˝ × 5˝. Every creature in the area takes 6-36 (6d6) points of damage. The cloud lingers and slowly cools, doing 4d6 damage on the second round and 2d6 on the third and last round. Saving throws apply for half damage every time. Fire-dwelling or fire-using creatures are naturally not harmed by the steam, unless dampness harms them.
  • Vapor: in one segment the wand pours out billows of warm, steamy vapor equal to a fog cloud 4˝ deep, 6˝ high, and 8˝ wide. It lasts 6 rounds and stays in place unless moved by magical or natural breezes or winds. Cold-using creatures take 1 point of damage per round inside it, and cold-dwelling creatures take twice that.

Experience points 4,500 · Sale value 25,000 gp · UA III.D.2

This prized charm is a specially blessed symbol that can turn undead as if a cleric were using his or her power to turn them. It looks ordinary at other times, but glows brightly when presented forcefully (like a holy symbol) in the presence of undead. Success is decided as for a cleric of a set level, which varies from amulet to amulet. Roll for the type when one is found:

Dice scoreEffective cleric level
01-305th
31-556th
56-757th
76-908th
91-009th
  • Wearing: it must be worn at all times to work. When it is not worn it becomes inert, and it stays inert for the first seven days after it is put on.
  • Value: 200 x.p. value and 1,000 gp sale value per effective cleric level.

Experience points 200/level · Sale value 1,000/level gp · UA III.E.6

This item looks like one of the small, rather weak miscellaneous magic items that are more often found, usually (though not always) one with a limited number of uses. On its possessor’s command, it suddenly changes into any other miscellaneous magic item except an artifact or relic; for instance, some form of Horn of Valhalla. Its limits:

  • No form can ever be repeated.
  • If the item copied is normally destroyed when used, the anything item is destroyed after that use too.
  • If the item copied has a short-term, single-use effect (such as a horn or drums), the anything item returns to its original form after one use of that power.
  • If the item copied has a long-term effect (such as a helm of underwater action), the magic lasts one day (24 hours).
  • In any case, the item disappears after three uses.

Experience points 4,000 · Sale value 40,000 gp · UA III.E.6

One of these small black spheres could be mistaken for an ordinary bead, a marble, or perhaps an unusually black, dull pearl. Each is about three-quarters of an inch across and quite heavy, weighing almost an ounce. From 5-8 are usually found together.

  • Throwing: a bead can be thrown up to 3˝.
  • Blast: on impact it releases a burst of force that does 5-20 (5d4) hit points of damage to every creature within a 10-foot radius of its center. Each victim may save vs. spell.
  • Save succeeds: the creature is thrown out of the blast area.
  • Save fails: after taking damage, the creature is enclosed in a sphere of force. The sphere forms around any and all such creatures in the 10-foot radius, even large ones, and lasts 3-12 rounds. Victims can escape only by the same means that would bring down a wall of force.

Experience points 200 ea. · Sale value 1,000 ea. gp · UA III.E.6

This well-made book is always small: usually no more than 12 inches tall, 6 inches wide, and 1 inch thick, and some are only 6 inches tall. Every one is very durable, waterproof, bound and locked with iron and silver, and gets +3 on its saving throws (as “leather or book”).

Its pages accept magic spells written on them, and it can hold up to 45 levels of spells, which makes it highly prized by all magic-users as a traveling spell book. One is almost never found at random with spells already in it, because owners guard fully or partly filled copies carefully.

Experience points 4,500 · Sale value 35,000 gp · UA III.E.6

These highly magical boots give the wearer several powers:

  • Snow: travel across snow at the normal movement rate, leaving no tracks.
  • Ice: travel at half the normal movement rate across even the most slippery ice without falling or slipping (horizontal surfaces only, not vertical or steeply sloped ones).
  • Warmth: the wearer stays warm and comfortable at temperatures as low as −50°F with only scant clothing (a loin cloth and cloak, for instance). Fully dressed in cold-weather clothing, he or she can withstand temperatures as low as −100°F.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 7,500 gp · UA III.E.6

On command, the wearer of these ordinary-looking boots can change the tracks he or she leaves. The basic power makes the wearer’s footprints anything from as small as a halfling’s to as large as an ogre’s, appearing bare or shod as desired. In addition, each pair can make the tracks of four of the following:

Die rollTrack print leftDie rollTrack print left
1basilisk9horse
2bear10lion (or giant lynx)
3boar11mule
4bull12rabbit
5camel13stag
6dog14tiger (or leopard)
7giant, hill15wolf
8goat16wyvern

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 7,500 gp · UA III.E.6

These boots always look like ordinary footwear; detect magic shows a faint aura of both enchantment and alteration. When the wearer concentrates on wanting to fly, wings sprout at the heels and he or she can fly without having to keep concentrating.

  • Daily limit: up to two hours per day, all at once or in one or more shorter flights. If the wearer tries to fly longer, the boots’ power fades quickly (but not suddenly) and the wearer slowly descends to the ground.
  • Recovery: for every 12 hours of unbroken non-use, the boots regain one hour of flying power, never more than the two-hour maximum.

Each pair is of a certain type:

Die rollFlying speedManeuverability class
115˝A
218˝B
321˝C
424˝D

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.E.6

These wrist bands look exactly like normal, non-magical protective wear. Worn by a character or creature able to use a bow, they make the wearer an excellent archer:

  • The wearer can use any bow (not crossbows) as if proficient with it, if not already.
  • With any type of bow the wearer is already proficient in, he or she gains +2 to hit and +1 damage whenever using that type of bow.
  • These bonuses add to all others, including those of a magic bow or magic arrows, except a bonus from weapon specialization.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · UA III.E.6

These wrist bands look ordinary, but they let the wearer move by brachiation: swinging from one tree limb, vine, etc. to the next. The power works only where such hand-holds exist.

  • Swinging movement: 3˝, 6˝, or 9˝; the more jungle-like the conditions, the faster the rate.
  • Climbing: the wearer can climb trees, vines, poles, ropes, etc. at 6˝, and swing on a rope, vine, or other hanging flexible object as if he or she were an ape or other simian.
  • Leaping: if desired, the wearer can leap and jump as if wearing boots of striding and springing, but each jump must end with grasping a rope or vine, moving through the upper parts of trees, climbing a tree or pole, or some other activity connected with brachiation.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 10,000 gp · UA III.E.6

This chime can be struck only once every turn, and its tone rings for three full rounds. While it rings, no spell with a verbal component can be cast within a 30-foot radius of it unless the caster makes a saving throw versus breath weapon.

After the ringing fades, the chime must rest for at least 7 rounds. If it is struck again before then, it makes no sound, and a full turn must pass from that moment before it can sound again.

Experience points 2,000 · Sale value 20,000 gp · UA III.E.6

This black cloak has great magical power; detect magic shows a strong alteration aura. The wearer gains:

  • Climbing: as if under a spider climb spell.
  • Webs: immunity to entrapment by webs of any sort. The wearer can move through them at the rate of the spider that made the web, or at a base rate of 6˝ otherwise.
  • Web spell: once per day, a double-sized web, as the 2nd-level magic-user spell.
  • Poison: +2 on all saving throws against arachnid poison.

Experience points 3,000 · Sale value 25,000 gp · UA III.E.6

Made of dark brown or black cloth, this cloak does not stand out as unusual. It radiates enchantment and alteration in equal measure.

  • Invisibility: 90% chance of being invisible while the wearer stays still in a shadowy or dark place. The wearer can hang upside down from a ceiling like a bat and keep the same chance.
  • Flight: holding the edges of the cloak, the wearer can fly at 15˝ (MC: B). Or the wearer may turn into an ordinary bat, along with everything worn or carried, and fly as one.
  • Flight limits: either kind of flight works only in darkness (under the night sky, or in a dark or nearly dark place underground). Each can be used for up to one hour at a time, and after a flight of either kind, of any length, the cloak gives no flying power for an equal period.
  • Protection: it also protects as a +2 robe of protection, even while the wearer is in bat form.

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 15,000 gp · UA III.E.6

This looks like an ordinary pointed hat and gives off a dim evocation aura. Any magic-user who has it can use it: point the small end at the ground and toss it forward with a spin given by moving the palms in opposite directions. The cone spins at blurring speed and grows into a small but very powerful whirlwind.

  • Size: 5 feet wide at the base, 15 feet wide at the top, and up to 45 feet high (depending on the ceiling or some other limiting factor).
  • Timing and movement: it appears 1-4 segments after the cone is thrown, then sweeps straight ahead at 18˝ for 1 full round, or until a solid, sturdy object breaks it up (a stone wall, very thick woods, etc.). A living thing that breaks it up takes damage as below.
  • Damage: creatures of under 2 + 1 hit dice caught in it when it forms, or touched by it along its path, are killed instantly and carried along. Other creatures caught in it or touched by it take 4-16 points of damage. Those within 5 feet of its outer edge when it forms take 2-8 points of damage.
  • One use: the cyclocone is destroyed when the whirlwind dissipates.

Experience points 300 · Sale value 15,000 gp · UA III.E.6

rolls.label: Caught in or touched by the whirlwind

system.description:
This looks like nothing more than a magic dart, but it is far more powerful. Once thrown, it multiplies in the air as it speeds toward its target, making an angry buzz like a swarm of hornets. When it is thrown, roll percentile dice for its bonus to hit and the number of darts it produces:

Dice rollBonus to hitNo. of darts
01-40+15-20 (5d4)
41-70+24-16 (4d4)
71-90+33-12 (3d4)
91-00+42-8 (2d4)

The bonus applies only to hitting, not to damage, which is the standard amount for an ordinary dart (1-3 vs. S or M, 1-2 vs. L).

Experience points 750 · Sale value 7,500 gp · UA III.E.6

This set of parchment cards is usually found in an ivory, leather, or wooden box. A full deck has 34 cards. When one is drawn at random and thrown down, it forms an illusion with sound and sight that lasts until dispelled.

  • The illusory creature will not go more than 30 feet from where the card landed, but otherwise moves and acts as if it were real. The illusions follow normal routines and respond to attacks; DMs should play them as if they were real creatures.
  • When the illusion is dispelled, the card becomes blank and cannot be used again.
  • Picking the card up from where it lies dispels the illusion automatically and instantly.

Jokers (2): an illusion of the deck’s owner. The other cards form four sets of eight (the suit names are not given in this text):

Experience points 1,500 · Sale value 15,000 gp · UA III.E.6

This clerical candlestick is a holder of specially alloyed metal with two arms: one of silver and mithral, bright and glittering, and the other of iron and adamantite, as dark and dead-looking as the first is bright. The arms twist together into a stem of alternating bright and dull bands, and the base spreads into eight legs of alternating silvery and black metal. It is about 1 foot tall and just over half as wide, and weighs between 30 and 40 gold pieces.

Candles: the dicerion gives off a faint aura of its own, but works magically only with specially made candles of the purest wax with finely powdered obsidian and crystal layered inside, both blessed and consecrated (see the 1st-level cleric spell ceremony). With a pair of these in its arms, the whole thing radiates a powerful aura. Both arms must hold tapers for any power to work, even when only one candle is lit.

  • Burning time: a special candle burns 5-8 turns in a gentle draft, such as that made by walking while holding the dicerion. A strong draft cuts this by 1-2 turns. Kept still and out of any breeze, a candle lasts 9-16 turns.

Both candles lit:

  • The cleric touching or holding the dicerion can see in any darkness, or in the brightest light, as if it were normal daylight.
  • On the cleric’s command, the candles instead give off a strange, metallic light that dispels all natural shadows (not the undead creature) within a 30-foot radius. While this power is used, the cleric loses the special sight described above.

Only the black arm’s candle lit: a sphere of darkness with a 15-foot radius surrounds the cleric. It does not hinder the cleric’s sight or movement, but it affects every other creature within the radius. If a bright light strikes the cleric’s eyes while in this state, he or she is blinded for 1-4 rounds.

Only the bright arm’s candle lit: a sphere of brilliant light surrounds the cleric, whose sight is unharmed as long as he or she touches or holds the dicerion. The light blinds creatures of darkness (evil) for 2-8 rounds; creatures of light (good) cannot look at the area without being blinded for 1-4 rounds. If magical darkness envelops the cleric while it works this way, he or she cannot see for 1-4 rounds.

Experience points 2,500 · Sale value 25,000 gp · UA III.E.6

This special dust has many uses:

  • Into water: a pinch thrown into a large body of water instantly turns 1 cubic yard of it to nothing. The pinch becomes a marble-sized pellet floating or resting where it was thrown. When this pellet is thrown down, it breaks and releases the same volume of water.
  • Sprinkled over an area (for example with a wave of the arm): it cancels a precipitation or cloudburst spell, or dries up as much as 1 cubic rod of water.
  • Against water creatures: a water elemental or similar creature must save versus spell or be destroyed. Even on a successful save it takes 6-30 points of damage.

The dust does not affect liquids that are not some form of water (fresh, salt, brackish, alkaline, etc.).

Quantity: a pouch holds 11-20 pinches. The dust can be sprinkled to dry up moisture only while at least half of the original number of pinches remains. Once less than half is left, sprinkling the rest has no effect.

Experience points 1,000 · Sale value 8,000 gp · UA III.E.6

rolls.label: Water creature on a save
rolls.note: Printed as 6-30 with no dice; no standard dice give exactly 6-30, so one 25-sided die is used.

system.description:
This plain powder looks rather like chalk dust or powdered graphite, until someone stares at it; then it clearly changes color and form under scrutiny.

A pinch makes the creature dusted appear to be any other creature of similar shape, up to 50% larger or smaller than its real size. For example, a halfling could look like a small human, a human like an ogre, a pegasus like a mule. An unwilling target may save versus spell to avoid it. The person sprinkling the dust must picture the desired illusion while shaking the powder over the subject.

  • Duration: 7-12 hours unless dispelled sooner.
  • Quantity: a typical pouch holds 11-20 pinches.

Experience points 10/pinch · Sale value 100/pinch gp · UA III.E.6

This ordinary-looking dust is a highly magical powder for hiding the passage of its owner and companions. Its use gives off no magical radiation. It is usually found in a finely sewn pouch holding 13-24 pinches.

  • In a room: a pinch tossed into the air makes a chamber of up to 1,000 square feet as dusty, dirty, and full of cobwebs as if it had been abandoned and unused for a decade.
  • On a trail: a pinch sprinkled along a trail wipes out the signs of passage of up to a dozen men and horses for a mile back.

Experience points 500 · Sale value 200/pinch gp · UA III.E.6

There are at least five sorts of these items, each stranger and more potent than the last. An egg of desire is a small oval object. When it is set on its large end and touched in a certain way, it starts to rock back and forth in rhythm, giving off a soft chiming sound. Once it is activated, any creature that sees it must save versus spell or fall under its magic. The viewing range is 20 feet.

EggEffectXP valueGP sale value
BlackHolds viewers permanently, unless circumstances allow the spell to be broken or they die.5005,000
BoneViewers place their most prized magic item before the egg, then leave and forget what happened.90010,000
CrystalViewers place all the gems they have before the egg, then leave and forget what happened.8009,000
GoldenViewers place all the precious metals they have before the egg, then leave and forget what happened.6004,000
ScarletHolds viewers for one minute, then makes them enraged so they attack the first living thing they see after the minute is up.7003,500
  • Removal: an egg’s effect can be removed only by dispel magic or remove curse.
  • Unintelligent creatures: even these can be affected, since each egg sends signals straight to the viewer’s brain. However, the Bone, Crystal, and Golden eggs affect creatures of under 7 intelligence differently: such a creature grabs any magic item, gems, etc. dropped by another victim (if there is one), covets what it took, and treats it as its most secret and valued treasure.
